articleTitle: Efficiency Optimization of Cu2O/CsSnGeI3/IGZO Perovskite Solar Cell using Simulation
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: One of the materials being investigated for use in solar cell applications is perovskite. However, because of their better efficiency, lead-based perovskites are being investigated extensively; however, they are not environmentally benign. Our suggested solar cell, which is based on cesium tin-germanium triiodide (CsSnGeI3), has a higher efficiency and poses no environmental risks. Because of its high electron and hole mobility for carrier transport, we have selected IGZO as the ETL and Cu2o as the HTL. The open-source SCAPS 1D framework is used to computationally optimize the solar cell for optimal efficiency. First, we created an idealized simulation of the solar cell. Later, for optimal efficiency, the thickness of the absorber layer and ETL was increased. To examine the effects, we have also changed the bulk and interface flaws at the boundaries and impact of fault variations on the cell's efficiency. In order to choose an appropriate metal contact, we have also changed the metal contact's work function. Efficiency of 24.61 %, open circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.99 V, fill factor (FF) of 87.85%, and short-circuit density (Jsc) of 24.86 mA/cm2 were obtained from the first simulation of the cell with optimal boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Log Periodic Slotted Tri-Band Antenna for Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Wearable antennas are pivotal in advancing healthcare monitoring, military communication, and IoT, offering seamless integration with fabrics and devices for realtime data transfer. High-frequency wearable antennas ensure compactness, enhanced performance, and reliable operation, making them indispensable in modern applications. This paper presents a circular patch antenna with dimensions 54.4 × 54.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, designed using a Teflon (PTFE) substrate of 1.6 mm thickness, known for its low loss, high thermal stability, and excellent dielectric properties. The design features log-periodic slots that enable multiband resonance at 11.99 GHz, 12.95 GHz, and 15.36 GHz, achieving return losses of -43.23 dB, -31.19 dB, and -22.80 dB, respectively, along with favorable VSWR, gain, and directivity. The antenna also demonstrates low Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) values, ensuring safety and reliable performance, measuring 1.23 W/kg, 1.20 W/kg, and 1.03 W/kg at 11.99 GHz, 12.95 GHz, and 15.36 GHz, respectively, for wearable applications in current practical use cases across various sectors.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Techniques to Detect a DDoS Attack in Flying AD-HOC Network
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Flying Ad-hoc Network (FANET) consists of aerial devices, such as Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), which work together to perform specific tasks. The system stands out because of its unique coverage, speed, and mobility capabilities. However, these features also make it vulnerable to various security threats, particularly in routing. One of the major threats to the availability of FANET is the Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) flooding attack. These threats generate excessive traffic on network node, which causes frequent delays, packet loss, connectivity issues, and failure in operation. In this paper, we delve into detecting DDoS attacks by monitoring traffic patterns. We simulate a DDoS flooding attack scenario and explore different Machine Learning (ML) techniques to enhance detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimizing Machine Learning Algorithms for Accurate Heart Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Heart disease is a leading global health challenge, emphasizing the need for effective diagnostic solutions. This study evaluated the accuracy of machine learning algorithms in heart disease diagnosis with the aim of finding the most reliable method. The algorithms examined contain Random Forest, Support Vector Classifier, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, Optimized Logistic Regression, SVM, Naive Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Trees, and SGD Classifier. Among them, optimized logistic regression and naive Bayes have the highest accuracy of up to 88.52%, demonstrating their predictive capabilities. The result of this work is optimized logistic regression and naive Bayes are capable of early detection of cardiovascular disease. Offering major perspective for integration into clinical practice. Future work will explore the refinement and real-world application of these models to further improve healthcare outcomes.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Dual-Band Antenna for C-Band and X-Band Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance evaluation of a compact dual-band microstrip patch antenna optimized for C-band (6.6 GHz) and X-band (8.5 GHz) applications. The proposed antenna integrates flipped Z-shaped slots to achieve precise dual-band resonance while maintaining a compact form factor. A full ground plane structure and Rogers RO5880 substrate are utilized to enhance radiation efficiency, impedance matching, and gain. The antenna is designed with a microstrip feedline to ensure optimal power transfer and minimal signal reflection. Simulation results demonstrate an excellent return loss of -68.317 dB at 6.6 GHz and -33.218 dB at 8.5 GHz, indicating strong impedance matching. The proposed design also achieves a gain of 7.015 dBi at 6.6 GHz and 5.312 dBi at 8.5 GHz, making it well-suited for satellite communication, radar systems, and high-frequency wireless applications.

articleTitle: Development and Validation of a Four-Electrode System for Impedance-Based Moisture Measurement in Concrete and Mortar
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The accurate monitoring of moisture content in concrete and mortar is critical for guaranteeing proper curing, drying, and long-term performance of building materials. This work describes the design and validation of a four-electrode device for impedance-based moisture monitoring. The electrodes, made of stainless steel for durability and corrosion resistance, were tuned in size and spacing to enable effective ionic interaction and consistent electrical readings. A low-frequency sinusoidal voltage signal of 10V (1–10 kHz) was delivered to the input electrodes, while the output electrodes assessed the resultant potential difference and related it to moisture content. The system was tested in regulated temperature and humidity settings, with measurements taken at predetermined intervals. The results showed a substantial link between moisture content and electrical impedance/conductivity, indicating that impedance rises.

articleTitle: Morse Code Based Two-Way Communication Device for Visually Impaired and Mute
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: People with disabilities like visual and speech impairments face significant challenges in interacting and communicating with others because conventional tools like smartphones are predominantly visual and verbal based. Consequently, such individuals depend on others even to convey simple messages. These problems restrict their ability to express themselves freely. Moreover, existing assistive technologies are complex and expensive making them impractical choice for widespread use. This project presents an innovative solution to overcome these obstacles: a Morse-code-based device that operates on a single-button interface thus making it extremely useful for people who can't see. This IOT-based device translates Morse code signals into text which is further displayed on mobile devices. Additionally, the message logs are preserved on cloud storage thus ensuring convenience and accessibility to the users. The morse code inputs are captured by the push button presses and then converted to readable text with the help of the microcontroller ESP8266, which further gives visual outputs through LCD and audio outputs through the buzzer. The device also supports two-way communication, that is two similar devices can send and receive messages from each other easily, thus even if two disabled people have to communicate with each other, they can do so without any difficulty. This function enables interaction between individuals with similar kinds of disabilities and fosters inclusivity and mutual understanding. It aims to promote independence and social engagement. The service is highly practical, cost-effective, and most importantly, easy to use.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Sn-Based Perovskite Solar Cell: Structure, Optical Properties, Design and Stability
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Perovskite SCs (PSCs) have gained considerable interest in progressive years due to their rapidly advancing power conversion efficiency (PCE), simple solution-based fabrication methods, lightweight and flexible designs, and versatility for wearable technologies and ultra-lightweight space applications. Their cost-effectiveness, stemming from the use of inexpensive materials, further enhances their appeal. Since their initial efficiency of 3.8% in 2009, PSCs have achieved a remarkable efficiency exceeding 25%, reflecting a growth of over 550%. Although efforts to enhance the stability of PSCs are reinforcing their potential for widespread adoption, concerns regarding lead toxicity have driven the pursuit of safer alternatives. Among these, Sn-based perovskites have emerged as a promising candidate. This article delves into the fundamental properties, operation mechanisms, and stability of Sn-based perovskites, highlighting their potential as a lead-free solution.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Fault-Tolerant Implementation of Quantum Logic
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The need to consider fault-tolerant quantum circuits is essential due to the intrinsic fragility of quantum systems. Recent studies have focused on optimizing complexity, resource utilization, and error resilience to enhance execution efficiency on quantum hardware. This paper performs a comparative analysis of fault-tolerant implementation approaches for quantum circuit design, emphasizing resource optimization, scalability, and error resilience. This paper illustrates recent designs that include enhanced Toffoli gate decompositions with reduced T-depths and resource-effective designs, demonstrating the tradeoffs among T-depth, T-gate count, and ancilla usage. These insights facilitate developing effective, scalable, and reliable quantum computing solutions, which are essential for both near-term quantum computation and future advancements.

articleTitle: A Simple Memristor Emulator Using only MOSFETs and a Grounded Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a memristor emulator circuit that utilizes six MOSFETs, implemented in the TSMC 180nm CMOS process. The proposed circuit operates at a voltage of ± 0.9V, LTspice simulations were conducted to verify operational performance, demonstrating reliable and repeatable memristor behavior under specified conditions. Compared to existing designs, the proposed emulator offers improved tunability while using fewer MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Faster R-CNN vs SSD: A Deep Learning Approach for Nodule Detection in Lung Cancer Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Deep learning-based object identification technology has numerous uses, including facial recognition, commercial analytics, and medical imaging analysis. An object detector has a backbone for extracting features and a head for classifying items and predicting bounding boxes. In this work, Single Shot Detector and Faster R-CNN are used as detectors for lung cancer diagnosis. Both these detectors were trained for nodule identification, and their outcomes were compared. The findings indicate that SSD attains an accuracy of 43.80% whereas Faster R-CNN achieves the accuracy of 95.80%.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of 4-bit and 8-bit Vedic Multipliers Using Variable Bit CSLA
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: A chip comprises many logic blocks and digital circuits, of which multiplier is one of the most common blocks Multipliers are fundamental components in digital circuits, widely used in microprocessors, computers, and image processing. As technology advances, optimizing power, speed, and area is crucial. Vedic Mathematics, known for its efficient computational techniques, provides a powerful approach to multiplier design. This study analyses 4-bit and 8-bit Vedic multipliers using various adders, emphasizing the superiority of the Variable Bit Carry Select Adder (CSLA) over conventional and inexact adders. Vedic multipliers, inspired by ancient mathematical principles, enhance computational efficiency by reducing delay and power consumption. The proposed multiplier achieves a 60% improvement in delay and an 80% reduction in power compared to conventional designs. The variable-bit CSLA optimizes carry propagation, significantly lowering computation time and power consumption while maintaining accuracy. These advancements make the Variable Bit CSLA a strong candidate for high-speed, energy-efficient applications, reinforcing its importance in next-generation digital circuits

articleTitle: Design of Instrumentation Amplifier for Pacemaker Using 180nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: A instrumentation amplifier (IA) has been designed for pacemakers, crucial for amplifying and filtering the heart's faint electrical signals (0.05 Hz to 50 Hz). Built using 180nm CMOS technology and simulated in Cadence Virtuoso, the IA boasts a gain of 167 dB, a 6.248 kHz gain-bandwidth, a 176° phase margin, and a 100 dB common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR). These performance metrics demonstrate that the designed IA meets the stringent requirements for implantable pacemaker, ensuring reliable and accurate signal processing for proper cardiac pacing.

articleTitle: Surface Plasmon Resonance-Based Optical Biosensors for Refractometric Sensing: A Theoretical Review
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: SPR-based optical biosensors, strengthened with Photonic Crystal Fibers (PCFs), are vital for tracking environmental conditions, ensuring food quality, and advancing biological diagnostics because of their remarkable ability to detect changes in the refractive index (RI). By integrating PCFs, these sensors achieve superior light propagation and field confinement, enabling tailored optical properties for optimized detection accuracy. Recent advancements in theoretical modeling, innovative designs, and material combinations have expanded their operational range and real-world applications, such as early disease detection, pollutant monitoring, and food quality assurance. Despite significant progress, challenges like improving sensitivity, miniaturization, and cost-effective production remain. Future innovations involving nanostructures, advanced coatings, and artificial intelligence aim to address these hurdles, paving the way for SPR-PCF biosensors to revolutionize optical sensing technologies.

articleTitle: Detecting Digital Financial Transaction Frauds Using CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The Unified Payments Interface has become increasingly popular as a convenient and user-friendly digital payment platform. However, the surge in Digital Transaction has also resulted in a rise in fraudulent activities, presenting a significant security challenge. This paper introduces a novel approach to detecting fraudulent Digital Transaction by leveraging convolutional neural networks (CNN). By incorporating the CNN model, this study aims to offer a cost-effective solution for identifying Digital Financial fraud. The CNN's ability to analyse patterns in data makes it particularly suitable for fraud detection in Digital Financial Transactions. We evaluate our proposed methodology using a comprehensive dataset that includes both fraudulent and genuine transactions. Our results demonstrate a significant improvement in fraud detection accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. This research contributes to the advancement of secure digital payment systems by presenting an innovative approach to detect fraud transactions. Financial institutions and payment service providers can utilize this methodology to enhance the security of Digital Financial Transactions and protect users from fraudulent activities.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Efficient 32-Bit Vedic Multiplier
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This proposed work specifies a version of the Vedic multiplier designed for large numbers using principles from the ancient technique of Vedic multiplication. A Vedic multiplier is a preferred choice as it demonstrates improvements in speed, area, hardware complexity, power consumption, and scalability. Implementation is performed using Verilog HDL on the Modelsim tool, while Xilinx is utilized for circuit architecture. This study examines three 32-bit Vedic multiplier designs-the Carry Save Adder, the Carry Lookahead Adder, and the Ripple Carry Adder-using various adder architectures. All three designs consumed similar power, approximately 0.082W. The 32-bit CLA-based Vedic multiplier is the fastest, with a delay of 26.466ns, and all had nearly identical power consumption. In terms of area utilization, the RCA-based multiplier was the most efficient Vedic multiplier. Index Terms—High-speed multiplication, Power consumption, Vedic mathematics, Parallel processing, Circuit design.

articleTitle: A Novel Secure and Scalable Framework for a Cloud-Based Electronic Health Record Management System
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Any hospital management system must include health records. However, because clinical institutions are sending largely health data, they have no way to control or maintain their own medical records. Electronic health records, or EHRs, are a systematic to collect electronic health information about specific individuals' patients or populations. Cloud computing is becoming an important aspect of the health operation. In this paper, we suggest a scalable and safe cloud-based system for managing electronic health records. The architecture enables patients and other medical stakeholders in healthcare institutions to access the EHR system through universal healthcare service providers using a range of devices in a contextual setting. This study examines the effectiveness of the cloud-based EHR system by taking into account important elements such as user access control, data integrity, and the confidentiality and availability of medical records. The suggested approach effectively addresses security issues, including the compromise of private health information.

articleTitle: Area and Delay Efficient Adders for Inexact Computing Implementation
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Recently, inexact computing has gained a lot of interest in modern computational systems since it can improve the use of resources particularly when the exact precision is not critical. Here, the proposed 24-bit Approximate Ripple Carry Adder (ARCA) features a hybrid design based on simplified logic operations that embed approximate computation for LSBs and exact computation for MSBs. This method significantly reduces the power consumption, footprint, and latency of traditional precision adders. Extensive simulations reveal that ARCA outperforms its competitors with regard to resource savings while preserving almost all the computational precision. The results clearly indicate that our approach reduces power consumption by 27%, delay by 29%, and area by 25% compared to traditional ripple carry adders. The above results demonstrate the effectiveness of ARCA in many resource-constrained applications, including embedded systems, digital signal processing, machine learning, and multimedia.

articleTitle: Efficient Energy Storage System for Renewable Energy Source Integration to Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: An efficient Energy Storage System (ESS) is essential for Renewable Energy Sources (RES) namely, solar and wind, which are intermittent and fluctuate with environmental conditions. ESS technologies, such as batteries enable grid stability by storing excess energy induced with high productivity and released throughout low volume of production. In this work proposes an efficient ESS for RES integration into the grid. The Photovoltaic (PV) system utilizes a High-Gain Z-Source Boost (HGZSB) converter, optimized through Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)-based Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm to extract maximum energy. In parallel, the Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG)-based Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS) are regulated by a PWM rectifier and a PI-controlled PWM generator to stabilize power flow. A bidirectional battery converter manages energy storage, enhancing stability and reliability by balancing supply-demand fluctuations. Artificial Neural Network (ANN) controllers are employed to control current and voltage levels, optimizing the overall system's dynamic response. Finally this work is implemented by using a MATLAB 2021a Simulink Software. The proposed HGZSBC achieves an efficiency of 94.5%.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Enhanced Asymmetric CPW-Fed Dual Band Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: An innovative asymmetric CPW-fed dual-band antenna augmented by machine learning is presented in this study. It is designed for wireless applications, particularly WLAN and WiMAX. The physical dimensions of the antenna were optimized to produce improved impedance matching, bandwidth, and radiation efficiency by incorporating machine learning techniques like KNN and Random Forest. The proposed antenna, which incorporates metamaterial structures, operates efficiently across its target frequency bands. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate a bandwidth increase from 0.36 GHz to 2.36 GHz, a gain improvement from 0.12 dBi to 0.54 dBi, and a return loss enhancement with values reaching -27.03 dB compared to traditional designs. These findings confirm the efficacy of ML-driven optimization in antenna design.

articleTitle: Smart Streetlight with Inbuilt Collision Warning System
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The daily aspect of road safety is extremely crucial since it is a component of every transport system. Everyone in the world is a road user directly or indirectly. The present transport system has reduced the distances but enhanced the dangers because of the bad infrastructure. Lakhs of road accidents occur annually, claiming countless lives and leaving millions injured seriously. This research addresses the use of microcontrollers and other sensor technologies that would be implemented on highways to enhance the road safety of travelers. The prime focus is to enhance the road safety by providing sufficient notice to the driver or rider about the hindrance in front of him in time. For this purpose, proximity infrared sensors have been placed in all streetlights on highways, hence when disturbances or obstacles are sensed, it produces a temporary electrical pulse. This is thereby sent between close-by streetlights to send word of the interference to approaching automobiles in time, alerting the driver or biker well beforehand. The system also includes an added module which has an integrated ultrasonic sensor placed within the vehicle for point-blank transmission and barrier recognition. Power-cutting options also exist on the streetlight system by auto-fading if it does not spot any vehicle inside the range of the within stipulated time. Experimental experiments have been conducted, and the efficiency of the suggested model is relatively higher than that of the current systems.

articleTitle: Monitoring Students in Online Learning Environments Using Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Since education is rapidly growing digital, it is more vital than ever to keep a check on students' online activity to make sure they are learning properly. The highly effective Convolutional Neural Network model introduced in this paper is specially developed to recognize student distractions in online learning settings with high precision and minimum processing cost. Our approach is perfect for real-time applications on low-processing-power computers since it uses fewer than 800,000 parameters and achieves an impressive accuracy of 96.13%, in contrast to classic models with many parameters. In order to detect subtle behavioral markers of student engagement and distraction without requiring a lot of computing resources, the proposed method uses a CNN architecture. The model's capacity to generate accurate predictions with low latency was validated through a series of tests conducted in online learning settings with a variety of student behaviors. Our study demonstrates that high-performance engagement monitoring is possible with reduced model complexity, adding a valuable tool for online platforms and educational organizations to enable focused, effective learning experiences. The proposed approach paves the way for future advancements in low-cost, highly accurate student monitoring systems and allows for further research into flexible learning environments.

articleTitle: Low Power Design Analysis of ALU Using FinFET
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper aims to provide a comparative analysis of low-power design methods for the implementation of the Arithmetic Logical Unit using Fin- Field Effective Transistor. The study evaluates four new important low-power methodologies: Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor, Gate Diffusion Input, Subthreshold and Adiabatic design. The paper aims to be the first of its kind to provide a comparative analysis using these four low-power models in FinFET Technology using the Cadence Virtuoso designing tool. FinFET, being a modern technology with lower power leakage than the conventional MOSFET, is being used in the four design models to test feasibility. These models showcase the practical implications of deploying these sophisticated models in an 8-bit Arithmetic logical unit to harness real-life use cases. The study investigates the tradeoff between the number of transistors required in each design, the power efficiency obtained, the area utilized, the delay, leakage current and the voltage transfer curve. The models are implemented in an ALU to understand how they would perform in real-world computational needs. We were able to obtain a reduction in power consumption of 76% provided by the Subthreshold Adiabatic Logic ALU and a decrease of 83% in the case of GDI based ALU. The findings contribute to understanding how FinFET 7nm technology can optimize power consumption for various digital applications, with potential benefits for both high-performance and low-power domains.

articleTitle: Orbital Angular Momentum-Enabled Free Space Optics Transmission: Impact of Indian Weather Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Free Space Optics (FSO) is a latest technology that has the ability for long-range data transmission. The range of transmission can be further be augmented via Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) multiplexing. We examine the performance of an OAM-enabled FSO system for the effect of diverse Indian air conditions. Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) beams are used as the OAM carriers in the proposed study. Four types of OAM modes, (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{LG}_{\mathbf{0.0}},\boldsymbol{LG}_{\mathbf{0,16}}, \boldsymbol{LG}_{\mathbf{0,32}}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{LG}_{\mathbf{0,64}}$</tex>), are parallel transmit data at a rate of 10 Gbps, resulting in a total transmission rate of 40 Gbps. We have utilized Bit Error Rate (BER), Q-factor, and eye diagrams as principal performance measures. The transmission is examined in four Indian cities-Chennai, Chandigarh, Jodhpur, and Srinagar-each having a distinct weather conditions. The demonstrated analysis reveals that range of information transmission are adversely affected by adverse weather condition, with highest ranges recorded as s: Chennai − 8 km, Jodhpur − 5.5 km, Chandigarh − 4.2 km, and Srinagar − 3.8 km. These differences are attributed to regional atmospheric conditions such as rain, drizzle, and haze, which can lead to compromising the effectiveness of the FSO link.

articleTitle: Power Reduction in NOT, AND and Full Adder Circuits Using Adiabatic Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The increasing demand for energy-efficient electronic systems has intensified research into reducing power dissipation in digital logic circuits. This study explores the application of adiabatic logic methods, namely Efficient Charge Recovery Logic (ECRL) and 2N-2N2P, to minimize power consumption. Adiabatic logic employs reversible computing principles to recover energy lost during switching, contrasting traditional CMOS circuits that dissipate energy as heat. This work implements and evaluates inverter, AND gate and full adders using these techniques. Simulations conducted in 45 nm and 180 nm technology nodes highlight significant power savings with adiabatic circuits compared to CMOS counterparts. ECRL demonstrates efficient charge recovery through cross-coupled PMOS and NMOS transistors, while 2N-2N2P offers enhanced energy recovery at lower frequencies. Results indicate a substantial reduction in average power dissipation, with ECRL achieving up to 66.70% power reduction in inverters and 57.33% in AND gates, while 2n-2n2p achieves up to 92% power reduction in AND gates and 37.04% in full adders. These findings affirm the potential of Adiabatic Logic for Energy-Efficient Applications in Portable Devices and sustainable digital systems. This study underscores the viability of these techniques in addressing the growing demand for energy-efficient electronics.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Energy-Efficient Approximate Multiplier and Wallace Tree Multiplier for Error-Tolerant Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The Wallace tree multiplier is a high-performance digital circuit optimized for efficient binary multiplication. It utilizes a hierarchical structure that reduces the number of adders and minimises critical path delay by summing partial products in a tree-like manner with half-adders and full-adders. Conventional multipliers are confronted with problems associated with high energy consumption and suboptimal area utilization, especially in energy-limited systems. Approximate multipliers can address these issues by balancing computational accuracy with efficiency, making them ideal for error-resilient applications. Two novel compressors architectures are introduced: an 8-transistor and a 14-transistor 4:2 compressor. This approach allows for faster computation compared to conventional array multipliers, making it well-suited for Error-Tolerant applications. The proposed multipliers are designed in Verilog HDL and evaluated through simulation on the Xilinx VIVADO 2018.3 design software, with the Artix-7 AC701 FPGA serving as the target platform. the approximate multiplier uses only 786 transistors, a 49% reduction in size compared to a traditional 1530-transistor Wallace multiplier and significant improvement in area (49 %), power (69.8%) and Accuracy (76%).

articleTitle: Automatic Modulation Recognition Using Modified Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: With the development of Deep Learning as a potent method for separating high-level representations from complex data, numerous fields have seen substantial progress. A crucial task in cognitive radio systems, spectrum sensing, and signal intelligence is automatic modulation recognition. The modulation type of a certain radio broadcast can be determined with the help of deep learning methods. In this study, we have used the RadioML 2016.10b dataset to evaluate the performance of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for automatic radio modulation recognition. The CNN architecture is tuned to optimize the performance. The combination of six convolutional layers and two dense layers gives an accuracy of approximately 93.334% at 12dB.

articleTitle: Enhanced Solar PV System with Battery Storage and Grid Integration Using Cascaded ANFIS-Based MPPT and Self-Lift Luo Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper proposes a Photovoltaic (PV) system integrating a Self-Lift Luo Converter along with cascaded ANFIS based Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) approach for electric charging (EV). The Self-Lift Luo Converter operates as DC-DC step-up converter utilizing voltage lift technique, which minimizes voltage stress on power switch and improves efficiency by employing low on-state resistance. To optimize energy extraction from the PV panels, cascaded ANFIS-based MPPT algorithm is implemented. The converted voltage is stored in a battery through Bidirectional DC-DC converter, facilitating efficient energy management and utilization. A three-phase voltage source inverter managed by Proportional Integral (PI) controller is used for transferring excess energy into the grid, guaranteeing steady and dependable power transfer. This integrated system not only maximizes energy utilization but also contributes to grid stability, offering a sustainable solution for renewable energy integration. MATLAB simulations are used to examine the system's performance, revealing quick and adaptable EV charging solutions.

articleTitle: Hybrid GAN-Based Transfer Learning Model for Advanced Threat Detection in Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In the realm of cloud computing, reliable detection of threats forms a very important aspect since systems might be at risk. In this research, they proposed a new model that incorporates GANs with transfer learning to allow for the development of accurate detection systems that can identify even the more concealed forms of hacks that are yet to be recognized. Data gathering encompasses compiling a large number of heterogeneous datasets, including historical attack data, network traffic logs, UNSW-NB15, and CICIDS, as well as those obtained from cloud service providers. A novel approach is then proposed that combines both steps: The first step involves the generation of synthetic data through GANs, and the second step involves improving the feature representation of the same. The utilization of the hybrid model has been demonstrated to have an astounding accuracy of 98% when it comes to the capability of recognizing both classic and new types of attacks, as indicated by the assessments. According to the comparative analysis of the results, the proposed hybrid approach that was provided has a higher level of efficiency compared to traditional threat detection systems while also having increased adaptability in different scenarios of cloud computing. This work not only makes a contribution to the improvement of cloud threat detection, but it also offers insights that may be used for the later development and applications of threat detection in a variety of cloud environments.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of SPR Sensor for Skin Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This MATLAB numerical simulation-based study carries out a novel SPR design of silver as the primary plasmonic material with lithium niobate and silicon nitride nanolayers for skin cancer cell detection. The SPR reflectance and resonance angle have been investigated using the transfer matrix method. At an operating wavelength of 633 nm, the proposed sensor's execution parameters, such as sensitivity, detection accuracy, and quality factor, are investigated. The reflectance spectra are analyzed using the angular interrogation method. The highest sensitivity for the proposed sensor was obtained at 302.5 deg/RIU.

articleTitle: Towards Energy-Efficient Optimized Localization in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are essential in monitoring the environment to gather real-time data. Localization of sensor nodes is crucial for efficient data information processing and transmission. The traditional localization techniques face many challenges, like high energy consumption and computational complexity, resulting in inefficacies in the outcome. To overcome the challenges of traditional localization techniques, this paper proposes an Optimized Energy-Efficient Localization Technique (OEELT) scheme. The proposed scheme is a combination of the Enhanced Distance Vector (DV-Hop) algorithm with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) algorithms. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme outperforms the state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy, energy consumption, and computation time. It reduces localization error to 4.56m, energy consumption from 0.85J to 0.51J, and improves the computation time from 2.4s to 1.5s.

articleTitle: Development of Generic Custom FILL Parameterized Cell
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In this paper, a new generic FILL PCell programmable layout created from scratch to satisfy the custom fill requirements is presented. Since it is currently not possible to generate FILL for RF devices (such as inductors, transformers, etc.) using PV tools, the idea is to create a technique that will allow designers to regulate FILL rather than relying solely on PV tools. To cater this requirement, uniform metal density should be there because it will minimize the impact of increasing resistance caused by thickness thinning due to erosion and dishing. It is possible to fill dummy cells inside RF devices in order to be compliant with metal density rules without degrading their electrical and magnetic performances.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm Modeling and Analysis of Acyclic Coloring in High Chromatic Graphs
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The acyclic coloring problem, a specialized area within graph coloring, has numerous applications across diverse fields. It involves assigning colors to the vertices of a graph such that no two adjacent vertices share the same color and no bichromatic cycles exist. This problem becomes particularly challenging in high chromatic graphs. In this paper, we introduce a genetic algorithm (GA) with structure-aware selection, crossover, and mutation operators to enhance performance on some benchmark graphs having high chromatic numbers. Compared to the state-of-the-art methods, the proposed GA achieves a 5% to 12.5% reduction in the acyclic chromatic number. Success rates remain high, exceeding 90% for queen graphs, 80% to 90% for Leighton graphs, and 70% to 80% for random graphs. High crossover rates, approximately 17000 to 20000 on an average, maintain diversity, while adaptive mutation strategies enhance convergence. These findings highlight the advantage of integrating structural awareness into evolutionary algorithms for efficient acyclic coloring solutions.

articleTitle: YoloNet: Hybrid YOLO11 and EfficientNet for Lumpy Skin Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD) is a very infectious and contagious disease which affects the lives of countless cattle each year. Machine/Deep Learning models like CNNs effectively detect this disease through images and track the progression of this disease in infected cattle. Various works have been done on this problem, using models such as MobileNetV2, ResNet50, Gradient Boost, Xception, Inception V3, and DenseNet121. This paper proposes a hybrid model, YoloNet, to detect the LSD virus in Cattle, using YOLO11 and EfficientNet-B0. The YoloNet model takes a pre-processed image and performs feature extraction using YOLO11 to generate a tensor. The generated tensor is given as input to EfficientNet-B0, which converts it to a feature map and classifies the image. The analysis of the YoloNet has been done on a dataset with 5 different classes of cattle, with 8014 total images. The accuracy of the YoloNet model, being 97.97<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, is significantly better than other pre-existing state-of-the-art models.

articleTitle: A Minimalist MOS-Based Meminductor Emulator Circuit
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: A simple grounded meminductor emulator (MIE) based on a MOSFET configuration is presented in this paper. With six MOSFETs and two capacitors, the proposed circuit may efficiently create pinched hysteresis loops (PHL) at frequencies up to 100 KHz. The dependability of the design is confirmed by thorough analyses that include PVT assessments, which refer to modeling chips at various process, voltage, and temperature corners and non-volatility testing. Simulations were performed with 180 nm CMOS technology characteristics in CST (Cadence Spectre Tool). The consumption of power is a few microwatts in the proposed MIE. A comparative analysis of existing designs illustrates the benefits of the proposed MIE circuit.

articleTitle: Innovative Approaches to Low-Cost Multiplier Design Using Approximate Computing and Clock Gating
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel design methodology for low-cost approximate radix-4 booth multipliers that significantly reduce energy consumption in error-tolerant signal processing applications. Unlike prior works that focus solely on either partial product generation (PPG) or partial product accumulation (PPA), our approach co-designs these units to balance approximation errors, resulting in an internal error mean that is nearly zero. This integration enables substantial energy savings while maintaining comparable accuracy to existing designs. To further enhance energy efficiency, we incorporate a Synthesized-based clock gating technique, reducing unnecessary switching activity in the design. Experimental evaluations on Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filtering and image classification tasks demonstrate that the proposed multiplier achieves up to 39.3% reduction in total power consumption while maintaining accuracy within an acceptable range for error-tolerant applications. Additionally, delay and area utilisation are reduced by approximately 15.18% and 8.26%, respectively, compared to the existing method. Compared to traditional accurate booth multipliers, our design provides a better trade-off between power efficiency and computational precision, making it a promising alternative for energy-constrained digital signal processing (DSP) systems.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Meta-Surface based Antenna for Ka-Band 5G Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In the recent technological development of the high-speed network, it is mandatory to have the reliable, secure, low loss and uninterrupted connection for various use cases in automotive and commercial industry. Circular Polarization in the antennas is one of the key features to minimize the losses and establish reliable connection. This article presents the single layer compact circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna with wide band impedance bandwidth and 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW). The proposed design exhibits 7.76 GHz of impedance bandwidth and 800 MHz of 3-dB ARBW in the Ka-band. The size of the overall design is 7 mm × 7mm × 0.5mm. Moreover, the design exhibits the peak gain of 4.79 dB and cross polarization discrimination (XPD) of around -20 dB. The proposed design is suitable for various automotive 5G applications.

articleTitle: Simulative Analysis of DSP-PDM-256-QAM-Enabled Free Space Optics Transmission: Impact of Rain and Fog Weather conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This research work presents a complete simulation-based analysis of a free-space optics (FSO) communication system that combines digital signal processing (DSP) with polarization-division multiplexing (PDM) and 256-QAM modulation. The performance of the system is assessed under different weather conditions, such as rain and fog. The design and evaluation are done using a simulation framework, with bit error rate (BER) and error vector magnitude (EVM) acting as the main performance parameters. Significant findings indicate that the system is able to transmit the data over a maximum distance of 1200 m in light fog, 700 m in moderate fog, and 550 m in heavy fog. Similarly, in rainfall conditions, the system provides data transmission over distances of 1600 m during light rain, 1250 m in moderate rain, and 750 m during heavy rain, all considering the EVM value below 3% and the BER value at or below 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>. These results explain the reliability and adaptability of the DSP-PDM-256-QAM-enabled FSO system throughout the challenging weather conditions, highlighting its suitability for implementation in difficult environments. The study gives a key understanding of optimizing FSO systems to combat harsh weather, laying the foundation for robust, high-performance communication networks.

articleTitle: Fidelity Analysis Under Different Noise Condition for Single Qubit Quantum Teleportation
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In the domain of quantum communication, quantum teleportation (QT) emerges as a pivotal protocol, enabling the transmission of quantum states across significant distances. However, the ubiquitous presence of quantum noise inevitably affects this process, causing deviations in the teleported state from its intended configuration. This study proposes an innovative approach to mitigate noise error (bit-flip and phase-flip) and within quantum channels. The method involves implementing quantum gates between communicating parties, effectively diminishing the impact of these noise types on the entangled channel and enhancing QT efficacy in noise-prone environments. Experimental results demonstrate that noisy channel has low-fidelity 16.67% in bit flip noise and 68.60% in phase flip noise. The proposed noise mitigation quantum circuit attained the 100% fidelity.

articleTitle: Implementation of a 4:1 Multiplexer Using Compact Modeled Flexible and Low Voltage OTFT for Realizing it as a Universal Logic Gate
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The article discusses the utilization of a previously developed organic thin-film transistor (OTFT) with flexibility and bending characteristics for the realization of complex circuits, such as the 4:1 multiplexer. This 4:1 multiplexer function as a universal gate capable of implementing various basic logic gates, including AND, OR, XOR, and XNOR. Silvaco TechModeler and Silvaco Gateway tools are employed for the compact modeling of the fabricated device and the implementation of the 4:1 multiplexer, respectively. The device operates at 1 V and demonstrates favorable performance parameters. Logic gates implemented using the 4:1 multiplexer exhibit favorable transient characteristics for all four possible logic inputs (00, 01, 10, and 11). The Silvaco TechModeler tool achieves compact modeling with approximately 100% accuracy (with an error of less than 1%) between experimental and modeled data. This solution-processed, cost-efficient, and compactly modeled device can be further utilized to realize various complex analog and digital circuits, as well as applications in medical sensing and wearable electronics. Furthermore, the 4:1 multiplexer circuit is expected to be used in the development of higher-order multiplexer circuits, ALU circuits, and other complex systems.

articleTitle: GDI and Dynamic Logic: A Synergy Behind the Modern Electronics
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The main goal of this work is to design a 2x2 multiplier as well as a full adder and featuring low power and low delay characteristics, which will be beneficial for creating a low-power arithmetic unit ideal for microprocessors. In order to evaluate the performance parameter, the Cadence Virtuoso software used the Stanford model file for CNTFET at a 32nm technology node. The proposed circuit explored the Dynamic Modified Gate Diffusion Input (DMGDI), a hybrid of Dynamic Logic Block (DLB) and Modified Gate Diffusion Input (MGDI). Since MGDI suffers from ratioed logic and threshold drop, resulting in inadequate swing for certain input combinations. Considering this, the paper proposes the Dynamic Modified Gate Diffusion Input (DMGDI) technique, which integrates DLB with MGDI, resulting in full swing output. The DMGDI-based full adder and 2-bit multiplier are constructed to illustrate the applicability. In comparison to the DGDI (Dynamic Gate Diffusion Input) based full adder and multiplier, the suggested circuitry reduced power consumption by 42.28% and 45.55%, respectively, while also decreasing delay by 30.4% and 42.17%. Thus, the PDP parameter decreased by 59.7% and 68.6% for the proposed DMGDI-based full adders and multipliers, respectively, in comparison to DGDI circuits, indicating the superiority of the recommended circuitry.

articleTitle: Electrode Polarization-Based Sensor for Real-Time Monitoring of Salt and Sugar Concentrations in Beverages
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: An electrode polarization impedance-based sensor was developed due to the increasing demand for accurate and non-invasive methods to monitor the level of sugar and salt in drinks. This sensor is based on the description of a reliable process of using a four-electrode system for measuring the levels of sugar and salt in various drinks. There are two pairs of electrodes in the system: the inner pair senses voltage, and the outer pair delivers a regulated AC signal. Ionic (salt) and non-ionic (sugar) molecules in the solution both affect the electrode polarization impedance (Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</inf>), and changes in voltage mirror these effects. As per experimental data, there exists a clear inverse relationship between the output voltage and sugar and salt content, which makes this method suitable for real-time monitoring of beverage composition. Sensitivity analysis of the sensor offers similar results for various beverages with increased sensitivity observed at increasing salt concentrations. The proposed method is a good tool for industry and research applications, as it presents a non-invasive, reliable, and cheap alternative to food safety management, health monitoring, and the soft drink industry.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Hybrid Framework for Early-Stage Prediction of Alzheimer Disease: A Predictive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Alzheimer Disease (AD) is a progressive neuro-degenerative disorder that impacts millions worldwide, presenting a considerable healthcare issue. Usually, symptoms start out mildly and get worse with time. Early identification is essential for effective treatments and decelerating disease development. Predictable diagnostic methods frequently show constraints in scalability and accuracy, requiring the development of advanced computational systems. This study introduces a Deep learning-based hybrid framework for the identification of reliable symptoms for the early prediction of AD. Deep Learning has become an essential tool in healthcare due to its ability to identify complex patterns in large datasets. This research combines two deep learning architectures: ResNet50 for feature extraction from medical images, such as MRI, and MobileNet for collecting temporal patterns, applied on the Alzheimer's OASIS dataset to detect early-stage Alzheimer's disease. The framework's performance is assessed using important metrics: sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy during the training, validation, and testing phases. This study emphasizes the significance of multidisciplinary deep learning methodologies in transforming early diagnosis and the possibility of hybrid deep learning strategies in progressing medical science to address intricate healthcare challenges.

articleTitle: Deep-Learning Based Aspect Sentiment Classification for Low-Resource Language
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Task of sentiment analysis is being increasingly recognized as an important one, not just from an academic but also from a business perspective. The bulk of the approaches that are now in use, make an effort to identify the overall polarity of a sentence, paragraph or text span, regardless of the entities that are addressed in the review. Aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) deals with sentiment at a fine level. In this paper, a deep learning based model of aspect sentiment classification (ASC) for low-resource language data is proposed. It is based on multiclass classification paradigm. The presented model employs a BiLSTM unit followed by a dense layer. Experimental results have yielded accuracy 72.03% for well-accepted IIT Patna Hindi dataset. This is higher than that of previously reported works for Hindi.

articleTitle: A Review on Energy-Efficient PCF Based Plasmonic Biosensors for Biosensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Creating sensitive and specific biosensors is essential for the early detection and controlling of diseases. This study introduces biosensors based on Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) and Photonic Crystal Fiber (PCF), aimed at diagnosis of various diseases. The sensor takes advantage of the distinctive features of a PCF and heightened the SPR's sensitivity to detect tiny changes in the Refractive Index (RI), which measures biological samples. A certain portion of a PCF structure is covered in a thin metal layer, allowing the excitation of surface plasmons when illuminated with light at certain wavelength or angle. The resonance condition, which is closely linked to the RI of the surrounding medium, shifts when disease biomarkers are present. This shift is tracked and analyzed to enable precise and real-time disease detection. Thus, this study reveals SPR biosensor's remarkable sensitivity and specificity, with potential for integration into portable diagnostic devices, making it a promising option for early disease detection and personalized healthcare.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a 1.2V OTA-Based Active Filters in 45nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Operational Transconductance Amplifiers (OTAs) play a vital role in modern analog circuit design, offering a flexible and efficient approach to signal processing by converting input voltage into output current. Unlike traditional operational amplifiers (Op-Amps), which generate voltage-based outputs, OTAs provide current-based responses, making them highly suitable for applications requiring tunable gain and high-speed performance. This paper presents the design and implementation of an active filter using an OTA in 45 nm CMOS technology, optimized for operation at a nominal supply voltage of 1.2V. The proposed OTA-based filters, including Low-Pass, High-Pass, Band-Pass, and Notch Filters, exhibit low power consumption, high gain, and enhanced bandwidth, outperforming conventional designs. Simulation results indicate that at 1.2V, the OTA achieves a gain of 95.37 dB, a bandwidth of 34.88 MHz, and a power consumption of 5.72 mW. Additionally, the study examines the impact of varying supply voltage on power, gain, and bandwidth, highlighting key trade-offs. By leveraging the advantages of OTA-based design, this work provides a highly efficient solution for filtering applications in low-voltage, high-performance electronic systems, making it well-suited for communication systems, biomedical instrumentation, and RF applications.

articleTitle: Theoretical Study of Refractive Index Sensing of Glucose Using Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The new Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) sensor proposed in this paper is designed for non-invasive glucose detection in urine samples, providing an alternative to conventional blood-based glucose monitoring techniques. The N-layer model has been used to compute the reflectance of p-polarized incident light for the most prevalent Kretschmann configuration. A 141.66 deg/RIU sensitivity with FoM of 38.38 RIU-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> has been observed. Future research could concentrate on shrinking the sensor for incorporation into portable devices to provide continuous and real-time glucose monitoring.

articleTitle: Development of Deep Learning Based Model for Efficient Diagnosis of Tympanic Membrane Infection and Referrals using Otoscopic Images
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Infections in the tympanic membrane (in middle ear) is a serious middle ear ailment that mostly occurs in infants and younger children. It generally occurs as a result of mucosal disorders that causes impact on middle ear mucosa. Therefore, it requires on-time treatment and therapeutics. This work investigates the use of Inception v4 model for precise detection of some specific disorders in middle ear by taking inputs of otoscopy images. Acute Otitis Media (AOM), Acute Suppurative Otitis Media (ASOM), Chronic Suppurative Otitis Media (CSOM), Myringosclerosis (MS), and Normal Tympanic Membrane (TM) are the five different image classifications that make up the dataset, which was gathered and validated from AIIMS Raipur Hospital. Every category includes carefully chosen images for training and testing and their numbers depending on the rarity of the disease. While segregating different OM types and MS from normal TMs, binary classification models achieved remarkable accuracy, outperforming 95%. A noteworthy accuracy of 96.88% was attained by the model using AOM vs Normal dataset. In addition to this, multi-class classification model successfully classified TMs into AOM, ASOM, CSOM, MS and Normal TM with an accuracy of 93.75 %

articleTitle: Plasmonic Sensor with Interconnected Dual Ring Resonator for Refractive Index Sensing
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This study proposes a highly sensitive plasmonic sensor utilizing a Metal-Insulator-Metal (MIM) waveguide incorporating a stub-connected circular dual-ring resonator. The sensor consists of two rectangular waveguides coupled with a stub-connected double ring resonator, where the electromagnetic (EM) wave appears at the output port only when resonance occurs within the resonator at a specific wavelength. The sensor's performance is assessed through computational modeling using the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) technique. The results reveal four distinct sensitivity peaks across the visible and near-infrared wavelength ranges. By refining geometrical parameters such as the radius of the ring, the optimized sensor achieves a peak sensitivity of 2063 nm/RIU around peak 4 in the near-infrared region. It's remarkable ability to identify even the tiniest shift in refractive index makes it highly effective for biosensing applications.

articleTitle: A High-Performance 64-Bit ALU for AI Applications Using Vedic Sutras and Adaptive Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The Arithmetic Logic Unit, an important part of a processor, performs arithmetic as well as logic computations. The demand for better performance in processors has resulted in improved computational algorithms and multifunctionality, so all processor cores now reside on a single chip, but this again results in high processing burdens. Consequently, coprocessors have been employed in offloading addition, multiplication, and DSP applications to reduce the burden and impact overall speed significantly. This work introduces a 64-bit ALU implemented based on the Vedic Mathematics using Sutras for high-speed calculations. An accuracy-configurable radix-4 adder is used to dynamically control accuracy. Power gating is implemented here in order to optimize performance and power efficiency. The work has been implemented with Verilog HDL and synthesized in Xilinx ISE. The result includes performance improvements over reduced delays.

articleTitle: IoT Enabled Smart Metering for Domestic Electrical Distribution System Using Arduino
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The primary objective is to help consumers use electricity more efficiently from the power grid to minimize their electricity bills. The system continuously monitors power consumption by household appliances and calculates the total energy usage, alerting consumers when they are approaching the current slab rate. As the consumption nears the slab rate, the system automatically initiates a phone call and sends an SMS alert to notify the user to reduce power consumption. An auxiliary load line is included to connect non-essential loads; when power consumption is about to exceed the slab rate, the auxiliary line is automatically disconnected, and the status is communicated to the user via SMS. For enhanced scalability, overall power consumption is monitored through cloud-based tracking.

articleTitle: A Deep Autoencoder Based Outlier Detection Model for Intrusion Detection Systems in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: With advancements in Wireless Sensor Network technologies, a large inflow of data is observed in the networks. Security threats have been rising in the recent years. These frequent security threats have created an urgency to upgrade the Intrusion Detection Systems to highly complex methods. Hence, increasing the computation overhead on the energy limited WSN nodes. These nodes sometimes undergo data or network anomalies while transmitting or receiving packets, creating outliers. In order to remove the outlier, a Hybrid Convolutional Neural Network, Fully Connected Network based Autoencoder has been proposed. The proposed algorithm successfully mitigated more than 31,000 outlier instances. Further, Random Forest classifier gave a high accuracy of 99.975% on the reduced dataset.

articleTitle: Maximizing Efficiency and Controlling Congestion in Interlinked Queueing Models for Integrated Voice and Data Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper introduces an interdependent tandem queueing model for communication networks. The model effectively transports voice and data traffic by adopting strong packet switching and multiplexing capabilities. Application of the bit-dropping scheme as the best congestion control mechanism in the network model encapsulates one of the primary thrusts of this study. Performance measures of statistical multiplexing are built in the research, e.g., approximating the correlated arrival and service processes to the Poisson process, an empirical model employed in the modeling of random events. Importantly, the study illustrates the practical advantages of interdependent communication networks. In particular, it shows their ability to decrease the average transmission delay, or the time for data to pass through the network, as well as buffer level fluctuation. These results show the potential of interdependent networks to optimize network efficiency, a significant issue in modern communication systems.

articleTitle: Hybrid Analysis of Agent-Tesla: A Prominent Malware as a Service
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Adaptation of Information Technology (IT) and Information Communication Technology (ICT) has increased the unsecured internet exposure to cyber-attackers. Cyber criminals are always vigilant and ready for exploiting the opportunities. Attackers always look forward for new techniques and tactics to gain initial access into victim's environment. Getting Initial access into targeted environment is one of the primitive step of cyber-attack. This Paper is covering one of the most prominent and active malware as a service provider, Agent-Tesla. It works as Initial Access Broker and info stealer via vulnerability exploitation and phishing techniques. A detailed study of Technique Tactics and Procedures (TTPs) and Modus Operandi used by Agent Tesla is covered in this research article. Further, malware analysis of Agent Tesla sample, covering static and hybrid analysis adds novelty to this research analysis. Also, proactive measures and precautionary steps to secure the ecosystem from such attack vectors are presented to safeguard the unsecure network.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of LUT Based Approximate Multiplier for Energy-Efficient Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: A 4×4 approximate multiplier based on LUTs is presented and implemented for digital signal processing applications, with the goal of streamlining energy consumption and improving performance. The proposed multiplier employs Look-Up Tables (LUTs) and carry chain techniques to balance accuracy and hardware efficiency. The design process involves dividing partial products into two LUT-implemented parts, followed by a final combination stage. Simulation results shows that significant improvements over conventional multipliers, with power savings of up to 70% and latency improvements of up to 40%. The proposed design achieves logic power consumption as low as 59 mW while maintaining acceptable accuracy for error-tolerant applications. Consequently, these results validate the proposed multiplier's effectiveness in reducing area usage, lowering power consumption, and increasing speed.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of a Microfluidic Biosensor for Selective Cell Control in Lab-on-Chip Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Biological cell analysis, detection, separation from blood samples is an important task in evaluation and information extraction in health care disease diagnostics. In such sensor the cells are required to be controlled and migrated in particular channel area or cell analysis zone of a lab-on-chip device. Dielectrophoresis based microfluidic lab-on-chip devices are well established for manipulating cell movement which is suitable for detection and analysis. In this research, a microfluidic Biosensor for biological cell trajectory control is presented for trajectory control of platelets and red blood cells by optimizing the voltage applied on electrodes. Cell trajectory control is performed based on cell diameter and cell polarization effect on cells. Result have shown that motion of both platelets and red blood cells can be selectively controlled using voltages on electrodes with specific scheme having in range -4V to 4V such that cells can be captured in desired outlet.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Dual-Gate Hybrid Structure of Pentacene/Graphene for Enhanced Electrical Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: A dual-gate organic thin-film transistor (OTFT) in-corporating a pentacene/graphene hybrid structure and graphene electrodes has been designed and simulated to optimize electrical performance. The TCAD-simulation utilizes bottom contacts, pentacene as the organic semiconductor, and Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> as the gate dielectric, resulting in enhanced charge carrier mobility, lower power consumption, and improved device stability. The simulation outcomes reveal an Ion of -1.082 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A},\ Ioff$</tex> of -93.99 A, and an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{on}/I_{off}$</tex> ratio of 1.151 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−7</sup>, alongside a sub-threshold swing of -139.50 V/decade and a threshold voltage of 0.249 V, ensuring effective current modulation and energy-efficient operation. The inclusion of graphene electrodes enhances charge injection and switching capabilities, making the hybrid OTFT a strong candidate for high-performance, flexible electronic applications. Moreover, the dual-gate architecture provides superior electrostatic control over the channel, mitigating short-channel effects and improving overall stability. The integration of graphene electrodes further enhances charge transport by reducing contact resistance, reinforcing the device's potential for next-generation flexible electronics.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of PVT Tolerant and Fast-Settling Wideband CP-PLL Frequency Synthesizer
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The design of a fast-settling, PVT-tolerant wideband charge pump-phase locked loop (CP-PLL) frequency synthesizer is introduced in this paper. A differential charge pump utilizing a bootstrapped structure technique is implemented to ensure low phase noise. A differential ring voltage-controlled-oscillator (VCO) is employed, offering a broad tuning range while maintaining excellent phase noise performance. The design also incorporates a programmable divider, adjustable between 16 and 31, at the VCO output to scale down the frequency. The CPPLL synthesizer supports a frequency range of 96 MHz to 5.2 GHz, achieving a locking time of less than 500 ns and a phase alignment error below 100 ps for a 60 MHz reference frequency and a divider value of 28. The entire PLL circuit is realized using SCLPDK 0.18 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu m$</tex> CMOS operation and function at a supply voltage of 1.8 V.

articleTitle: Interleaved Boost Converter with Optimized MPPT Approach for Renewable Energy Based Propulsion System of EV
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Human civilization is based on transportation, which is essential to social advancement, economic growth, and global connectivity. While fossil fuel vehicles have been the backbone of transportation for over a century, their drawbacks have become increasingly evident in terms of environmental sustainability and public health. Therefore, a sustainable and efficient way of addressing these issues is to include Renewable Energy Sources (RESs), also known as green energy sources or alternative energy sources, into the network architecture. Therefore, this paper proposes a renewable energy - based propulsion system for Electric Vehicles (EVs) using Interleaved Boost Converter (IBC) and an optimized MPPT approach. The Photovoltaic (PV) system provides power that is allowed to IBC, and it works to current sharing between stages, which reduces the thermal stress on individual components, improving reliability. Additionally, by continuously adapting to fluctuations in surroundings, an MPPT based on Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) tracks the maximum power point more precisely. After converting the incoming DC power, the 3-phase Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) provides AC to the three-phase source. A Brush Less DC (BLDC) motor is achieved by the power use of a PI controller. The simulation is implemented in MATLAB Simulink. In contrast to WOA techniques, the results indicate that the proposed system offers excellent performance and improves the overall system efficiency.

articleTitle: Advanced SEPIC Converter and Fuzzy Logic Approach for RES Integration in Resilient Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In this research, a novel high gain Enhanced Single Ended Primary Inductor Converter (SEPIC) converter is presented. The solar array is connected to Enhanced SEPIC converter in the proposed system architecture. The rotor windings of a Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) are connected to a converter via slip rings, while the stator windings are connected to the grid. For applications like renewable energy systems and battery-powered gadgets, enhanced SEPIC converters are made to increase power conversion efficiency while offering larger input voltage ranges and improved control. To regulate power flow and provide stability inside the microgrid, Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) is managed by a Proportional Integral (PI). Robust performance under fluctuating load circumstances is maintained through the Fuzzy Logic Controller's (FLC) adaptive control, which is handle nonlinearities and uncertainties inside the microgrid. Power integration and conversion from DC to AC that is adequate for grid compatibility are ensured by the three phase VSI, which is managed by the PI controller. This methodology presents a viable resolution for dependable and sustainable microgrid structures, able to satiate the growing need for Renewable Energy resources (RES) while preserving grid effectiveness and stability. The efficiency of the Enhanced SEPIC converter is 92.5% obtained.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Spatial Diversity Techniques in Log-Normal Shadowing Channels
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This study explores the effectiveness of spatial diversity techniques in log-normal shadowing channels, which are crucial for enhancing the reliability and efficiency of wireless communication systems. Extensive simulation and analysis are done to investigate different spatial diversity techniques i.e. maximal ratio combining (MRC), space-time block codes (STBC) and selection combining (SC) in combination with different signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and shadowing variance conditions.
