We evaluate the effectiveness of the techniques through performance metrics including Bit Error Rate (BER), spectral efficiency, and signal-to-noise ratio. The results show that MRC and STBC perform better in most scenarios, which highlight the necessity of antenna diversity for system reliability and spectral efficiency. These findings while signaling the possible future enhancements of the wireless communication systems working under shadowed propagation environments are of paramount value in optimizing the system designs.

articleTitle: MIF-SWT-AD: Medical Image Fusion Using Stationary Wavelet Transform, Adaptive Feature Selection and Anisotropic Diffusion
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Image fusion is a crucial technique in multi-modal imaging applications such as medical diagnostics, where integrating complementary information from different imaging modalities (e.g., Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Computed Tomography (CT), Single Photon Emission Computed Tomography (SPECT), and Positron Emission Tomography (PET) etc. to improve clinical diagnosis and decision-making. This paper presents a hybrid image fusion method (MIF-SWT-AD) based on Stationary Wavelet Transform (SWT), incorporating Variance-Based Approximation coefficients (ACs) Fusion, Local Energy-Based Detail coefficients (DCs) Fusion, and Anisotropic Diffusion (AD) Filtering for post-processing step. The MIF-SWT-AD decomposes input images using SWT to obtain multi-resolution sub-bands (ACs, and DCs). The ACs are fused using a variance-based weighting strategy, ensuring dominant structural information retention, while the detail coefficients (DCs) are fused using local energy-based selection, preserving crucial edge and texture features. Finally, AD filtering is applied to the fused image for noise reduction and edge enhancement. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior fusion quality compared to conventional fusion techniques, The proposed method effectively balances feature retention, noise suppression, and visual enhancement, making it a promising approach for high-quality image fusion applications.

articleTitle: Optimizing IoT Network Longevity Through Super Node Integration and Multi-Hop LEACH Protocol
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimized Low Energy Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy protocol for IoT networks that maintains integration of the super node with multi-hop routing to enhance the longevity and efficiency of the network. Our designed model involves a subset of nodes such as super nodes having significantly more energy reserves than other nodes in the LEACH protocols. Involving multi-hop communications in the protocol will reduce the consumption of energy at the individual nodal level and improve the efficiency of data transmission. Our results show dramatic improvement in the life span of the network. It was noticed that the first node death occurs 29% later than the traditional LEACH setups. Moreover, this design enhances the total operational life span of the network by 269%, which reflects the paramount interest of implementing super nodes and multi-hop strategies. But these improvements come with a cost; namely, with an increase of 227%, on average, more energy is consumed per round. Results These results show strong trade-offs between the lifetime of the extended network and energy consumption, and a significant improvement over the baseline protocol.

articleTitle: Improved Positive Feedback Source Coupled Logic Based Tri-State Buffer and Its Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: An improved PFSCL tri-state buffer design for low-voltage and low-power applications using Dynamic Threshold Voltage MOSFETs (DTMOS) is presented in this work. By using DTMOS transistors for traditional pull-down transistors, the suggested design lowers the threshold voltage and total supply voltage needs. Due to this development, the circuit can function at a lower supply voltage of 1.4 V. With applications shown in bus realization and D-Latch configurations, a comparison analysis between the proposed PFSCL tri-state buffer and available designs is carried out to evaluate the efficacy of the proposed design. Through comprehensive SPICE simulations using 45nm GPDK CMOS technology parameters, the functionality of both designs is confirmed.

articleTitle: Design Innovations in TFETS: Enhancing Performance and Sensitivity Through Charged Plasma, Dual-Gate, and Work Function Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In recent years, Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors (TFETs) have garnered considerable attention as promising candidates to achieve the new generation of electronics that require high performance, low power, and scalability as they can provide increased energy efficiency due to the band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) mechanism and have a steep subthreshold slope. Nonetheless, the standard TFETs suffer from low on-state current along with short-channel effects and processing difficulties. However, to exploit these emerging potentials and improve TFET performance and capabilities junction less TFET, dual material gate, heterojunction architectures and driven work-function engineering innovations have arisen creating room for the use of TFETs in biosensing applications as well as high-frequency circuit designs. This review highlights four of the most significant advancements that comprise: Junction less and Core-Shell Nanotube TFETs for high-sensitivity detection of label-free biomolecules, Dual- Material Gate Heterojunction TFETs for enhanced on current and switching speeds, Symmetric Double-Gate Charge Plasma TFETs for simplified doping-less fabrication, and Drain Work Function Engineered TFETs to enable ambipolar suppression and improve RF performance. We then analyze the structure, functions, and applications as well the tradeoffs in terms of scalability, stability and reliability for each design.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Solar Powered IoT Based Livestock Fencing with Repeller Device for Smart Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The goal of this solar-powered livestock fencing with Internet of Things (IoT) based system is to protect crops from animal encroachment in a non-toxic and ecologically friendly manner. The system integrates sensors such as PIR and ultrasonic to detect animal movement and triggering a low-voltage electric fence with a repeller device to deter animals without causing harm. A camera provides real-time images, but GSM and Wi-Fi modules enable remote monitoring and notifications through mobile devices. The system, which is fueled by renewable solar energy, offers a sustainable solution for smart agriculture through automated and networked technology, improving crop protection, reducing animal injuries, and increasing farm management efficiency.

articleTitle: Analyzing Scaling Effects and Reliability Concerns in a Pre-Amplifier-Based Dynamic-Latch Comparator for Future High-Speed ADCs
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)

The study aim is to analyze the performance characteristics of dynamic and conventional comparators in relation to their capacity to reduce in size while maintaining constant functionality and dependability under thermal limitations that are common in low-power circumstances. For 0.1V <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta \text{Vin}$</tex> the delay / power obtained is 29.67% drop in delay and 8.89% more power absorption for the same temperature conditions. The applications of comparator are multipurpose parts used in monitoring, control, and signal processing etc.

articleTitle: 32×40 Gbps WDM Based FSO Transmission System for 5G Communication Services
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Designed to reach a total transmission capacity of 1.28 Tbps with each channel running at 40 Gbps, this work proposes a 32-channel Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) based Free Space Optical (FSO) communication system. Under a variety of meteorological conditions-including clear weather and fog-the performance of the proposed system is assessed using the Q-factor and bit error rate (BER). Reliable data transmission across a 50 km FSO link in clear conditions is shown by simulation results; performance declines to transmission distances of 3000 m, 1700 m, and 1260 m in light, medium, and heavy fog, respectively. These results underline the system's dependability and viability for high-volume communication, thereby stressing its capacity to help next-generation 5G wireless networks to be implemented.

articleTitle: Enhancing Congestion Management in WDM Networks: A Comparative Study of ROADM Architectures
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This research examines the effectiveness of Recon-figurable Optical Add-Drop Multiplexer (ROADM) technology in mitigating congestion within Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) networks, specifically focusing on a 4×4 channel configuration. Two key approaches-Wavelength Blocker (WB) and Wavelength Cross-Connect (WXC)-are assessed for their influence on network performance. Simulation results obtained through OptiSystem indicate that the WB delivers superior performance, with an average Q-factor improvement of 12% and lower Bit Error Rates (BER) compared to WXC, demonstrating its capability to provide higher signal quality and ensure error-free transmission. Both methods maintain strong optical signal integrity, as reflected in stable power levels (−13.4 dBm) and minimal noise (−46 dBm) across all wavelengths. The study further confirms that ROADMs play a crucial role in reducing congestion, enhancing throughput, and supporting network scalability, making them essential for high-demand optical networks. These results highlight the potential of ROADMs with innovative technologies to significantly improve network efficiency, especially in applications such as cloud computing and real-time services that require low latency.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a 1-Bit Full Adder Utilizing a Novel Grounded Keeper XOR-XNOR Circuit
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Ahstract-A novel hybrid-CMOS logic-style full adder design is presented in this study. To achieve good performance low-energy operations served as the basis for our study into hybrid-CMOS design. Several CMOS logic type circuits are employed in hybrid-CMOS design to create new full adders with the required performance. Both full adders employed in this study, based on a novel 8- T grounded based-keeper XOR-XNOR circuit. The use of a grounded keeper circuit transistor in the proposed study helps prevent charge leakage. Compared to its contemporaries, this circuit output exhibits a power-delay product (PDP) improvement of 35%-55%. Cadence Virtuoso is used to simulate each circuit in the 45nm GPDK CMOS manufacturing technology for transient analysis.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Blind Identification of Channel Coding Schemes
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The signal identification in blind radio frequency environment is gaining increasing importance in intelligent wireless communication systems. In this paper, we present a deep learning based blind identification of channel coding schemes. These include Convolutional coding, Turbo coding, and Low Density Parity Check coding-promising schemes for wireless communication systems. We have synthesized the dataset through MatLab simulations, where the randomly generated bits are encoded using specified coding schemes and modulated with BPSK and QPSK. The transmission of data has been simulated over a signal to noise ratio range of 0-20 dB in an AWGN channel, facilitating robust model training. Finally, a convolutional gated recurrent unit deep neural network is proposed. Unlike existing deep learning-based coding detection algorithms that handle only one modulation scheme, the proposed model processes information bits modulated with two different schemes. The method demonstrates average prediction accuracy approaching 87% to 90% over low regions of signal to noise ratio of the communication links.

articleTitle: Bounded Flux-Based Modelling of the Memristor and Implementation of Hybrid CMOS-Memristor Read-Write Circuit
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This manuscript presents the development, verification, and practical application of an oxide-based memristor behavioural model in Verilog-A, incorporating the resistive switching and bounded flux properties of memristors. Parameters like the mobility of oxygen vacancies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{\varphi})$</tex>, length of the device (D), and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}_{\mathbf{off}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}_{\text{on}}$</tex> parameters indeed depend on the nature of the material. Depending on these parameters, the device can respond to high-frequency and low-frequency input pulses. The developed memristor behavioural model captures the dynamic behaviour of memristive devices by combining the essential features of resistive switching and bounded flux. Through extensive simulations and in-depth discussions, the accuracy of the model is verified, and various read-and-write methodologies are explored and analysed. To showcase the practical application of the model, a read-and-write circuit is designed using pass transistors (CMOS) and memristors. Leveraging the resistive switching and bounded flux properties, the circuit is optimised to achieve efficient read and write operations. The functionality and performance of the circuit are verified using the Cadence Virtuoso simulator, ensuring its adherence to the expected behaviour based on the memristor behavioural model.

articleTitle: MIF-SWT-TVM: A Hybrid Multi-Modal Medical Image Fusion Using Stationary Wavelet Transform and Gradient-Based Total Variation Minimization
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The Multi-Modal Medical Image Fusion (M3IF) plays a critical task in combining corresponding important information from different imaging modalities (e.g., Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Computed Tomography (CT), Positron Emission Tomography (PET) etc. to improve clinical diagnosis and decision-making. This paper proposes a hybrid image fusion technique (MIF-SWT- TVM) that leverages Stationary Wavelet Transform (SWT) and Total Variation (TV) Minimization to enhance the visual quality and diagnostic accuracy of fused medical images. The method fuses approximation coefficients (ACs) using an averaging strategy and detail coefficients (DCs) using an absolute maximum selection strategy. The TV regularization is applied post-fusion to reduce noise, suppress artifacts, and enhance structural continuity, leading to a more refined and clearer fused image. The MIF-SWT-TVM is compared with some of the traditional wavelet-based and other fusion techniques, demonstrating superior preservation of anatomical structures and contrast enhancement. The MIF-SWT- TVM effectively enhances diagnostic features, reduces noise, and provides better visual quality compared to existing fusion techniques.

articleTitle: Automated Disease Detection of Rice Crops Through Video Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Rice is a standard in over 50% of the world's population, yet its cultivation faces severe losses of 20-40% due to various diseases. Timely and accurate disease detection is crucial for effective management and higher yields. Traditional visual inspection is impractical due to scale and cost, necessitating advanced approaches. Presents efficient solutions based on deep learning. Use a deeper folding network and faster R-CNN combination to accurately identify and classify rice blade diseases. The video based detectors are the VGG19 based portion is learned by an adjusted transfer learning machine-learning approach comprising of grouped components that allude to a custom- made prosthesis backbone. Finally, the model is tested on rice leaf images and videos, surprising the results of VGG16 and YOLOv3 in terms of disease-classifiction accuracy and video-based detection, respectively. Finally, Mask R-CNN is investigated to identify more than one disease, achieving a maximum accuracy of 96% for blast, Brown Spot, and Sheath Blight. Millions of farmers can benefit from such technology and in light of that a survey of CNN techniques used for rice disease detection was thoroughly reviewed. These methods promise advances in disease management, improved yields of rice, and overall food security worldwide.

articleTitle: A Simulation Study of InP/Si Heterostructure for Sensing in the NIR Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper presents a highly sensitive and selective InP/Si photodetector tailored for detecting 830 nm wavelength light. A comprehensive simulation analysis of the InP/Si heterostructure has been conducted to assess its optical performance across a wide spectrum of light. The optical characteristics of the resulting device are being evaluated by using a broad light source with an optical power of ~1 mW. The device's optical performance has been quantified in terms of responsivity and sensitivity. The responsivity of the proposed device has been measured under 830 nm illumination and bias voltages of -3 V, -2 V, and -1 V, yielding values of 2.4 mA/W, 1.9 mA/W, and 1.4 mA/W, respectively. These impressive performance metrics, coupled with the compact and low design complexity of the device, position it as a promising candidate for applications in the optoelectronics industry.

articleTitle: Mapping Student Understanding: Analyzing Concept Maps Using Network Similarity Measures
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This study explores the use of Network Analysis as a method to evaluate student-generated concept maps. By treating concept maps as networks, network analysis techniques are applied to assess the structural and relational aspects of the maps, providing insights into students' understanding and knowledge organization. The approach highlights key concepts, relationships, and patterns, offering a quantitative framework for evaluating the depth and coherence of student learning from student constructed concept map and concept map derived from student responses to a quiz. Comparing student-generated maps with an instructor's reference map offers valuable insights into both fundamental understanding and deeper conceptual comprehension. This innovative method has the potential to enhance educational assessments and inform teaching strategies.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Floating-Point Multiplier Employing Carry-Lookahead Adders
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: For hardware implementation of digital signal processing algorithms, the key components are multipliers. The design of multipliers plays an important role in overall system architecture. For algorithms requiring a dynamic range of data, floating-point representation is favoured over fixed-point. Nevertheless, floating-point multipliers provide difficulties for designers because of the large latency and space that they need. In this work, we suggest a more efficient method of floatingpoint multiplication with respect to both time and space. The bottleneck in the floating-point multiplier design is the Mantissa multiplication which is implemented through fast tree multipliers. Instead of using half-adders and full-adders as in conventional Wallace or Dadda tree multipliers, Carry-lookahead adders are used as compressors in the proposed structure, which resulted in a better partial product reduction in mantissa multiplication. The proposed design is validated through FPGA implementation using Verilog HDL description. It was observed that an improvement of 8.5% with respect to Wallace and an improvement of 9.9% with respect to Dadda is obtained in terms of latency.

articleTitle: Development of Piezoelectric Sensor Using PVDF/PMMA/PSSA Blend
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In this research, we developed a custom flexible piezoelectric sensor by constructing PVDF/PMMA/PSSA blends using a solvent casting method. This work concerns the fabrication and characterization of the piezoelectric sensor fabricated from polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) and polystyrene sulfonic acid (PSSA). PVDF has always been one of the best piezoelectric material, while PMMA contributes for the mechanical strength and PSSA adds to the electrical conductivity. Some of the characteristics that are measured within the 20Hz-10MHz frequency range are piezoelectricity, dissipation factor, dielectric, and conductivity. The enhanced piezoelectric response shown by the blended sensor compared to pure PVDF is attributed to the combination of PMMA and PSSA interactions with PVDF. It has been demonstrated that this blend shows promise for flexible piezoelectric sensors because of its enhanced mechanical and electrical properties.

articleTitle: Design and validation of Mixed Logic 2-to-4 Decoders Using 32nm FinFET Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper introduces the design and implementation of a 2×4 decoder using FinFET technology at the 32nm process node, leveraging transmission gate logic and dual-value logic to optimize performance. LP (Low power) and LPI(Low power inversion), HP(High Power) and HPI(High Power Inversion) 2×4 decoder is an essential combinational circuit widely used in digital systems for address decoding, de-multiplexing, and control applications. FinFETs offer enhanced electrostatic control and reduced leakage currents, addressing the challenges of traditional MOSFETs at nanoscale dimensions. By incorporating transmission gates, the proposed design minimizes propagation delay and power dissipation, such as 1.06u, static power=101p, dynamic 4.2u and delay offered 560ps achieving high-speed and energy-efficient operation. The use of dual-value logic further reduces the transistor count, leading to a compact layout with optimized area utilization. Simulation results validate the performance of the proposed design, demonstrating significant improvements in power efficiency, delay, and overall reliability compared to conventional CMOS-based decoders. The combination of FinFET technology, transmission gate logic, and dual-value logic highlights a novel approach to designing robust digital circuits in advanced technology nodes.

articleTitle: Keystroke Dynamics Based User Authentication Focusing on Fixed Text Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Protecting sensitive information has become highly critical in the digital age as traditional authentication methods like passwords and PINs are susceptible to theft and brute-force attacks. Even though physical biometric systems, such as fingerprints, iris scans, and facial recognition, offer better security, they usually demand expensive hardware and remain prone to spoofing techniques, such as fake fingerprints, voice recordings, and deepfakes. Behavioral biometrics, which analyzes user interaction patterns such as keystroke dynamics, provides a more secure and user-friendly alternative by focusing on unique typing behaviors. This paper introduces a hybrid CNN-LSTM architecture designed to effectively capture both spatial patterns and temporal dependencies in keystroke dynamics data. The proposed model aims to enhance authentication accuracy while maintaining usability, offering a robust solution to modern security challenges.

articleTitle: Design of 5G mm-Wave Patch Antenna with Ultra Low Return Loss Using Rogers RT5880
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: 5G wireless cellular systems are made to meet smartphone user's needs at millimeter wave bands. 5G is the fifth generation, which is reliable, fast and advanced. Better than the 4G wireless technology. The CST-MW simulator is used to study and simulate our antenna structure for 5G communication and it's uses. For 5G purposes, the primary focus of this work is to study the design of a micro-strip antenna with a micro-strip feed line working at a Resonant frequency of 25.78 GHz. We choose Rogers RT-5880 substrate material, which has a 0.787 mm as it's substrate height, 0.0009 as it's loss tangent and 2.2 as it's dielectric constant (ε). It is possible for using the suggested structure in 5G applications. For 5G applications, it is highly reliable and efficient. Thus, a good return loss of-51.94 dB, enhanced 4 GHz bandwidth, 10 dB high gain, outstanding nearly 100% antenna radiation efficiency has been obtained in the antenna our design.

articleTitle: Latency-Aware Network Slicing for 5G URLLC Applications: Design and Optimization Strategies
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The growing need for 5G URLLC applications has led to the development of new network slicing techniques that are focused on very low latency and ultra-high reliability. This paper proposes network slicing with the collaboration of dynamic Resource Controller (ReCon) based on machine learning, which delivers full performance in diverse scenarios like smart city for autonomous driving, telemedicine remote surgery or industrial grade automation. Compared to state-of-the-art solutions, the proposed method yields large latency reductions and increased robustness in speed as well as additional improvements of reliability. By adjusting to changes in the network and efficiently handling connections between devices, this strategy is also positioning us well for growth: as usage increases and new applications are brought on board. Analysis and simulations cover what the approach can do for 5G network performance, showing it as a benchmark in network optimization and add further on with next-generation of Network Slicing advancements.

articleTitle: Analysis and Modeling of Electrical Parameters in OTFTs with BGTC Configuration
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The modeling of electrical parameters in organic thin-film transistors (OTFTs) using the Poole-Frenkel model, with the aim of optimizing the balance between dynamic and static performance aspects. A novel and efficient method is introduced to effectively capture significant nonlinear behaviors in these devices, offering a simplified approach without requiring an in-depth exploration of the internal mechanisms. The device structures investigated include bottom-gate top-contact (BGTC) configurations, in which pentacene is vacuum-deposited as the semiconductor material. The structure is completed with metal gates and a gate dielectric, both fabricated at room temperature, ensuring compatibility with low-cost manufacturing processes. The channel dimensions of the OTFTs are set at a width of 10 mm and a length of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5 \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. To analyze the device behavior, finite element simulations were conducted using the Silvaco 2-D Atlas simulator, providing insights into key electrical parameters such as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\text{on}}, I_{\text{off}}$</tex>, subthreshold swing (SS), and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\text{on}}/ I_{\text{off}}$</tex> ratio. The simulation results reveal a significant reduction in the drain-source current, attributed to the limitations in charge carrier mobility within the pentacene semiconductor. Additionally, the impact of varying gate and drain voltages on device performance was evaluated, highlighting the role of material properties and structure in optimizing OTFT efficiency. This work contributes to the ongoing development of high-performance, cost-effective organic semiconductor devices, with a focus on enhancing their overall functionality and application potential in next-generation flexible electronics.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Regular Polygonal Patch Antennas for Band Classification Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of machine learning models in classifying the number of frequency bands in microstrip patch antennas based on geometric parameters. The patches range from triangular to circular, with key input features being cut width, feed width, and patch size. The dataset, derived from High-Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) simulations, ensures precise antenna parameter measurements across a frequency range of 2 to 7 GHz. Four machine learning models—Support Vector Classifier (SVC), Random Forest, Extra Trees, and KNearest Neighbors (KNN)—were analyzed for their classification accuracy across different patch geometries. Results indicate that ensemble models such as Extra Trees and Random Forest outperform other classifiers, achieving the highest accuracy in predicting up to three bands. Additionally, hexagonal, octagonal and circular patches exhibited superior classification performance compared to triangular and pentagonal patches.

articleTitle: AI-Powered VLSI Design Automation for Faster Chip Production in Emerging Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The optimization techniques used in conventional VLSI design automation are rule-based and limited, which results in ineffective process execution and mistake detection. By using machine learning (ML) methods like Random Forest Regression (RFR), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Reinforcement Learning (RL), AI-powered VLSI design automation overcomes these constraints. Traditional design techniques are unable to keep up with next-generation semiconductor technology, which calls for AI-driven methods. The proposed approach increases accuracy and efficiency while decreasing human participation by automating many design processes. Experimental findings show a 20-30% reduction in power usage and a 50% reduction in design time (e.g., 75 hours vs. 120 hours for high-complexity designs) as compared to traditional approaches. The approach significantly reduces error rates by more than 60% and increases answer generation quality, attaining 89% accuracy for high-complexity designs compared to 75% in previous techniques. These improvements in design accuracy, scalability, and power efficiency represent a major step toward more effective automation of semiconductor design.

articleTitle: Autonomous Vehicle Traffic Flow Optimization Using AI and 5G Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Real-time optimization of autonomous vehicle (AV) traffic flow using 5G communication networks and AI algorithms could overcome the limitations of static traffic enforcement, which uses outdated technologies to manage fluctuating traffic demands. It allows dynamic flow. Such commodities cannot adapt in real time because to their rigorous handling requirements, which disrupts traffic dynamics and creates construction delays and traffic congestion. The study suggests transmitting real-time vehicle status data to nearest intelligent crossings via vehicular wireless networks (VWNs). These intersections enhance traffic flow and reduce 5G network congestion using AI algorithms. Predictive analytics will help AVs change routes while on the road to maximize travel efficiency. It finds that peak congestion, average route duration, and fuel use reduce vehicle CO2 emissions by 66.7%, 22%, and 15%, respectively. It determined that the proposed system was a viable design route for a deployable smart city transportation solution because it outperformed traditional techniques in economic and environmental criteria.

articleTitle: Optimizing Renewable Energy Distribution in Smart Microgrids Using IoT and Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Smart microgrids improve energy efficiency by integrating renewable energy sources, but their intermittent nature complicates steady power distribution. This research introduces an IoT-enabled Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for optimizing renewable energy distribution in smart microgrids. IoT sensors collect real-time data on energy production, use, and environmental variables, enabling adaptive management. The RL model adaptively acquires optimum energy distribution techniques to attain load equilibrium, energy storage enhancement, and grid stability. The system uses autonomous decision-making to reduce energy waste, increase cost efficiency, and enhance resilience. The proposed system facilitates real-time demand response, optimizes power distribution, and assures effective use of distributed energy resources. Experimental findings illustrate the efficacy of RL in mitigating uncertainty in energy supply and demand. This research advances the development of intelligent, self-adaptive microgrids, enabling a more sustainable and efficient energy infrastructure. Previous studies will investigate hybrid AI models to enhance performance further.

articleTitle: HEMT Based Different Structures for High Threshold and Breakdown Voltages: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The present review delves into the latest developments in High-Electron-Mobility Transistors (HEMTs), emphasizing the improvement of both the breakover voltage (Vbr) and threshold voltage (Vth). Several methods for modulating electric fields and lowering parasitic unwanted current are explored, including the use of composite step-like design gate structures with charge balancing plate and p-GaN buried layers. Further research is done on double AlGaN barrier designs, showing that reducing the amount of Al in the bottom barrier can lower 2DEG density and improve gate control, which raises Vth. The performance of enhancement -mode HEMTs is further enhanced by optimizations including graded AlGaN barriers, recessed gate designs, p-GaN caps, and the addition of dielectric layers like A1303. These methods ensure acceptable transconductance and saturation current while striking a compromise between high turn-on voltage (switching voltage) and breakover voltage.

articleTitle: Adaptive Portfolio Management in Volatile Markets Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Asset prices are highly volatile as the market is driven by macro-economic events, sentiments and geopolitics, a lot of time is spent understanding the changing dynamics to be one step ahead in making investment and trading calls. Traditionally, these dynamic conditions have caused troubles to the traditional portfolio management system, which is based on static models, to allocate suboptimally. Such limitations are addressed in this research by using Deep Reinforcement Learning real time portfolio optimization earning (DRL). Specifically, we explore three DRL algorithms: Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C), Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), Proximal Policy Optimization(PPO). In this research, the DDPG outperforms the others in terms of its annual return 23.1%, the PPO has the highest Sharpe ratio 0.998 for risk adjusted returns and A2C achieves long-term stability with balanced risk.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study on Multiple Object Detection and Tracking in Videos Under Complex Environments Using Advanced Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Multiple Object detection and tracking is a predominant area in computer vision and has numerous applications, including healthcare monitoring, autonomous driving, and anomaly detection. The proposed study is focused on multiple object detection and tracking under complex environments using advanced deep learning frameworks. Multiple object detection from videos under complex environments presents several challenges due to the dynamic and unpredictable nature of real-world conditions. The study summarizes the state-of-the-art methods, including important algorithms, datasets, and assessment measures, making it a fundamental resource for scholars and practitioners. It also highlights the shortcomings and difficulties in current solutions, offering information about areas that need more research. In conclusion, this study highlights new developments and approaches for the future, promoting the creation of innovative models and frameworks that can tackle outstanding problems in object tracking and detection.

articleTitle: Color and Defect Detection in Industry Automation for Real Time Intelligent Product Sorting
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper presents a real-time object sorting system that classifies objects based on color and detects surface defects in an intelligent manner for multi-purpose application like autonomous vehicles, supply chain, robotics and so on. The proposed system uses state-of-the-art camera module to capture images of objects and processes them through computer vision to classify items based on color and defect status. The captured images are compared against a custom dataset of labeled samples to ensure accuracy. Based on performance metrics, the intelligent CNN algorithm demonstrates superior classification accuracy compared to RFC, especially in complex scenarios. The edge processor module controls sorting mechanism, where servos actuate to direct objects into designated bins based on classification results. The research work illustrates exploring the potential of machine learning algorithm in automated quality assurance, offering scalable, adaptable, and efficient solutions for industrial applications.

articleTitle: Improving Error Resilience in FPGA-Based Multi-Level Approximate Multipliers Using Modified Full Adders
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The study provides a novel technique of increasing the tolerance error for FPGAs-dependent multi-level approximate multipliers, in the application of multiplexers along with modified complete adders. Resource usage should be optimized, and circuit simplicity must be improved at last. Although complete adders are critical to the arithmetic operations of digital circuits, the number of adders can increase the amount of power consumed, the amount of space required, and the process time. The proposed design enhances energy efficiency, reduces signal propagation time, and enhances defect tolerance by employing a multiplexer-based adder architecture. The optimized full adder significantly reduces the power consumption up to 27.7%, space utilization up to 22.9%, and gate count up to 22.8% as compared with traditional designs through extensive simulations. The design is suitable for applications that can afford a moderate amount of error as the error rate is less than 5%. This approach provides a long-term, effective, and extensible solution for systems that are constructed using field-programmable gate arrays, all while optimizing power, speed, and dependability for contemporary digital applications.

articleTitle: Automated Crop Harvesting with Robotics Using AI
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: “Automated Crop Harvesting using Robotics and AI” research may truly change the future of modern farming. New Robot Systems Integrated with Smarter Artificial Intelligence So the objective for making self-operating harvesters that can move around fields and find ripe crops using advanced machine vision and executing selective harvesting accurately. Among them, the project on real-time data from Using environmental sensors and AI-driven predictive analytics, the system hopes to improve harvesting. operations, increase crop yield, reduce waste. Innovation addresses pivotal issues such as labour Shortages and high operational costs while promoting sustainable farming practices. Ultimately, this project It works toward making farming better, ensuring that food is produced in a more reliable and efficient way. Also, this project considers how these technologies can work with farm management systems to Provides full monitoring and control. The all-inclusive method not only makes immediate harvesting better. Tasks and also helps with long-term farming plans and managing resources. By encouraging with new developments in robots and AI, the project aims to create better ways in farming technology, opening the This is the way forward to smart farming, the future.

articleTitle: Automated Detection and Classification of Pulmonary Lung Diseases Using Falcon Optimized BiLSTM Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: An automated and accurate detection of pulmonary lung diseases has become increasingly critical due to the rising global incidence of illnesses like lung cancer, pneumonia, and Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). Manual analysis of medical images is often time consuming, highlighting the urgent demand for efficient solutions in medical imaging. To address this, the proposed work develops a Deep Learning (DL) based methods for classification of pulmonary lung diseases. The preprocessing steps, including image augmentation, resizing, normalization, and data splitting is essential to ensure the lung images are appropriately prepared for further analysis. K-means clustering based segmentation is employed for isolating the relevant regions of interest for disease classification. For classification, a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network is utilized to capture both temporal and spatial dependencies in the lung images. To further enhance the performance of BiLSTM model, it is fine-tuned using Falcon Optimization Algorithm (FOA), improving classification accuracy of (96%) prediction. The validation from the python software outcomes addressing the need for improved diagnostic capabilities in healthcare.

articleTitle: Crow Search Algorithm for Energy-Efficient UAV Path Planning in Large-Scale Aerial Surveys
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: UAVs have been extremely influential for applications such as remote/sensing, disaster response, surveillance, and infrastructure monitoring. They are valuable in modern-day operations because they can conduct high-precision aerial surveys autonomously. Most of the existing trajectory planning approaches are based on metaheuristic algorithms of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), which are capable of providing satisfactory results. Still, they are computationally expensive with slow convergence and sensitive to local optima. In this paper, the challenges raised above are addressed by an Optimized Trajectory Planning Framework based on the Crow Search Algorithm (CSA). It is based on a nature-inspired optimization technique that mimics the intelligent foraging behavior of crows. The proposed approach dynamically adjusts the UAV flight path by balancing the exploration and exploitation, to compute the optimal trajectory quickly and meanwhile to save energy and avoid the obstacle. Unlike other metaheuristic methods, the Crow Search Algorithm does not confront the premature convergence problem and can guarantee adaptive path optimization even under uncertain environmental conditions. Results show that the energy efficiency performance of the Crow Search Algorithm is 15 percent better, the performance in terms of coverage is 20 percent improved, and the speed of convergence is 30 percent faster compared to various state-of-the-art methods. These experimental findings demonstrate that integrating CSA into UAV trajectory planning offers high computational efficiency, obstacle avoidance, and mission endurance, rendering it a superior UAV trajectory planning algorithm for real-time aerial navigation and autonomous surveillance applications.

articleTitle: Broad Band Access in Rural Areas: Bridging the Digital Divide Through Technological Innovations
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The digital divide persists in rural regions due to insufficient internet connectivity, limiting access to crucial services like education, healthcare, and economic prospects. A cost-effective and scalable approach to address this issue involves utilizing existing cable TV infrastructure to create a hybrid broadband network. This study introduces an innovative Hybrid Wired-Wireless Mesh Network model that combines Data Over Cable Service Interface Specification (DOCSIS) technology with Wi-Fi 6 Mesh Topology to deliver fast, dependable internet access. The proposed method repurposes cable TV lines as a wired foundation, complemented by strategically placed wireless nodes for final-mile connectivity. A Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite backhaul ensures high-capacity data transmission to isolated areas. Notable innovations include the implementation of Ethernet-over-Coaxial (EoC) adapters for smooth integration, solar-powered nodes for environmental sustainability, and edge caching servers to maximize bandwidth efficiency. The proposed solution not only bridges the connectivity gap but also empowers rural communities with access to telemedicine, e-learning, and digital marketplaces, fostering socio-economic development.

IEEE Keywords: Data over cable service interface specification

articleTitle: Efficient Sequence Modeling in Time-Domain Speech Enhancement Using MP-RNN
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Recent advancements in deep neural networks for speech enhancement emphasize the advantages of time-domain methods over traditional time-frequency techniques. However, processing long input sequences remains challenging due to computational limitations. The Multi Path-Recurrent Neural Network (MP-RNN) architecture overcomes this by partitioning long sequences into smaller, overlapping segments, enhancing computational efficiency and reducing optimization complexity. By integrating MP-RNN into the Time-domain-Audio-Separation-Network (Tas-Net), replacing conventional neural network modules, significant performance gains are achieved, with a reduction in model size by approximately 11 times on the WSJ0-2mix dataset. The performance is further evaluated under reverberant and noisy conditions, demonstrating the robustness of the MP-RNN architecture. Spectrogram and Power Spectral Density (PSD) analyses reveal noticeable improvements in signal clarity, with reduced noise and enhanced frequency representation in the processed signals. MP-RNN achieves a 7.89% improvement in Scale Invariant Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SI-SNR) and a 10.32% improvement in Signal-to-Distortion Ratio improvement (SDRi) over the Temporal Convolution Network (TCN). These results underscore MP-RNN's ability to efficiently handle long sequences, offering a scalable solution for real-world speech processing tasks.

articleTitle: Design of Pelletizer Automation based Embedded System for Soap Oil Factory
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: A SIBY Solvents Extraction Private Limited (Soap Oil factory) located near Chinna Salem has a major problem in Pelletizer control. This problem mainly depends on load control like handling coal and other raw materials by the conveyor.An embedded system based design consists of a controller which is used to measure the current and voltage rating for the Pelletizer. Based on the above parameters the power of the motors can be calculated simultaneously. The solution of the problem is solved by setting the lower limit and upper limit of current value for the motor. If the motor current is greater than set value the contactor, will cut the power supply to the motor. If the motor current less than set value it generates the on signal to the motor. In addition with that the on time and off time of the motor will be stored to the controller for the future reference. IoT based Monitoring is implemented here. The workers from the industry can't control the pelletizer within in a time due to its control panel distance and lack of language communication.

articleTitle: Advanced UART Verification Framework Using UVM and SystemVerilog
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Reliable communication is essential to operating 5G-integrated systems such as self-driving vehicles and sophisticated healthcare technologies. UART protocols use UVM for error checking, enabling full-duplex communication with baud rates of up to 128,000 with variable baud rates, as well as user-reconfigurable parameters, including a 58-bit data word, parity checking, and optional stop-bit settings. Verification is executed with Xilinx Vivado for synthesis and deployment operations and simulation by EDA Playground. The solution provides a 28.8% decrease in slice LUT usage, 94% dynamic power efficiency at 1.303W, static power of 0.084W, and a propagation delay of 0.256ns. Optimizations enhance system performance by increasing power efficiency and accuracy. The framework demonstrates exceptional scalability and reusability, which is a vital resource for real-time embedded systems.

articleTitle: Faces in the Fog: A Deep Dive into Face De-Identification Techniques and Their Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Face de-identification have drawn a lot of attention due to growing privacy concerns and the growing requirement for anonymization in visual data. This review suggests a systematic exploration of current face de-identification methods, emphasizing three main deep learning-based methods: diffusion models, latent Variable based transformations, and GAN-based models. The in-depth analysis of this literature provides a comparison of how well each strategies protect privacy while retaining data utility by focusing on the advantages and disadvantages of them. Our analysis delves deeper into the benefits and limitations of these models, focusing on important issues such as adversarial robustness, systematic biases, and trade-offs between realistic image generation and privacy preservation. This comprehensive overview synthesizes data from several studies, identifies important gaps in existing approaches and provides guidance to researchers and industry practitioners directing to more reliable and ethical de-identification frameworks.

articleTitle: Optimized Text-to-Image Synthesis Using Stable Diffusion and the Diffusers Library
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Text-to-image generation makes pictures from content, making a difference in areas like media, promoting, and instruction. In any case, to get precise pictures from the given content accurately had been a challenge, as numerous models make non aliased or wrong comes about. A few strategies exist for text-to-image generation, counting GAN-based models, which utilize ill-disposed preparing to refine picture quality, and VAE-based strategies, which encode content into a inactive space but frequently struggle with high-resolution points of interest. Ordinary models face challenges in semantic arrangement and regularly generate low-fidelity or artifact-prone pictures. Stable Diffusion mitigates these confinements through progressive denoising, parameterized control, and computational effectiveness, enabling high-resolution and semantically coherent outputs. This study employments Stable Diffusion with the Diffusers package to produce high-quality images by turning content into visual patterns and refining them with user controls. The pictures are tried for clarity, exactness, and productivity, appearing that Stable Diffusion can make important visuals.

articleTitle: Netflix Recommendation System by Genre Categories Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The ascent of web-based features, customized content suggestion is one of the basic elements improving client commitment and maintenance. This paper presents a thorough investigation of the Netflix proposal framework, which puts together its forecasts with respect to AI and cooperative separating from conduct information about the watchers' inclinations. It consolidates the two methods into a half breed way to deal with make customized proposals. It further sharpened the framework utilizing the technique of Singular Value Decomposition with upgraded exactness for proposals pertinent to the watcher. This is acknowledged by dynamism by which it is feasible to learn through the models that the watchers' preferences change over the long haul by include designing and procedures in light of profound learning. Consequently, there is arrangement with genuine watcher inclinations at the more exact level. This exploration shows and portrays how these procedures efficiently pursue further developing watcher fulfillment, and consequently fundamentally contribute towards the upper hand of an organization like Netflix, inside the exceptionally cutthroat streaming business sector. The review gives prime thoughts and rules to advance into future headway in regards to the proposal framework in streaming stages.

articleTitle: Remote Patient Monitoring System with Wearable IoT Devices and Biosensors for Vital Signs
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Due to infrequent patient monitoring and the reactive character of the traditional healthcare system, delayed diagnoses and inadequate management of chronic diseases are common outcomes. The study presents a solution to these drawbacks: a Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) system that combines advanced biosensors with wearable IoT devices to track vital signs continuously. By ensuring proactive healthcare through real-time data collecting and analysis, the entire system overcomes the drawbacks of conventional techniques. Early anomaly detection and timely medical interventions are made possible by the method's utilization of scalable cloud infrastructure and advanced machine learning (ML) methods, such as CNNs (Convolutional Neural Networks) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs). The proposed system achieves a 90% early detection rate, 95% sensitivity, 97% specificity in anomaly detection, and 92% patient satisfaction, which is a substantial improvement over existing techniques, according to the results. It also exhibits better vital sign measurement accuracy than existing systems, indicating its potential to completely transform patient care through better results and economical resource utilization.

articleTitle: Advancing Human Detection in UAV-Based Search and Rescue Using Transfer Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In rapid emergency situations, accurate detection of humans is essential for effective search and rescue operations, especially when using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) for quick response. This paper explores the performance of state-of-the-art You Only Look Once (YOLO) algorithms in identifying individuals in complex disaster scenarios. By utilizing the Combination to Application (C2A) dataset, that provides a diverse range of synthetic images depicting people in challenging environments, including floods, forests, fires, and collapsed buildings. Among the models evaluated, YOLOv11 demonstrated highest accuracy and robustness in detecting people across varied positions and backgrounds. By leveraging transfer learning, this approach achieved a precision of 92%, showcasing significant improvements in human detection. This study also highlights the potential of advanced algorithms like YOLOv11 to enhance the speed and accuracy of victim identification during UAV-assisted search and rescue missions in disaster-stricken areas.

articleTitle: Quantum Edge Cloud Computing: Revolutionizing IoT
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The augmented growth of the Internet of things (IoT) has brought an enormous surge in data generation requiring highly efficient, secure and scalable computational architectures. While conventional cloud computing is a widely used solution, it struggles with various issues like bandwidth constraints, latency and security vulnerabilities. Edge computing alleviates some of these concerns by processing the data closer to its source but time and again it is limited by restricted computational power. Quantum Edge Cloud Computing (QECC) presents a groundbreaking approach by assimilating the power of quantum computing with edge and cloud infrastructure to improve IoT performance. This study caverns the synergy between quantum computing, cloud computing and edge computing, foregrounding how this synergy can strengthen the IoT ecosystems. It examines the advantage of quantum assisted edge-cloud frameworks, investigates the advancements in cyber security through cryptographic methods and discusses plausible real-world applications. Additionally, the paper also features existing technological challenges, traces future research directions and suggests strategies required to realize a truly secure, intelligent and adaptive computing framework for IoT.

articleTitle: A Survey on Intelligent Reconfigurable/Reflecting Surface in 6G Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Intelligent Reflecting/Re-configurable surfaces (IRSs) aligns and regulates the wireless network environment and efficiently controls the wavefront (Phase, Amplitude, Frequency, Polarization). Given the recent emphasis on establishing a secure, cost-efficient 6G network, IRS can potentially be a key factor in establishing 6G wireless network from urban to remote areas. It has emerged to be a highly promising technology. The survey paper classifies the recent research investigations on IRS into various different yet important categories. For IRS aided vehicular communications, the paper presents a detailed analysis on the development, impact and effects on V2X, V2V and UAV communications. The paper also includes a detailed analysis on Machine Learning models for IRS based wireless communication towards 6G, which highlights the complex problems in wireless communication such as beamforming. The paper covers major categories related to deployment, future works and challenges etc.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Large Language Models: ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Claude and Qwen
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In recent times, Artificial Intelligence sector has been booming. Its applications are stunning and outperform the previous generation models as advancements happen. Machine Learning is one of the best methods to achieve Artificial Intelligence, and one of the most famous examples of this is the LLMs (Large Language Models). Recently, there have been breakthroughs in the LLM industry with the entrance of many models, such as OpenAI's ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Claude, and Qwen. In this article, we have conducted a detailed analysis of different LLMs. The priority is on the comparison of ChatGPT, Qwen, DeepSeek, and Claude. This paper informs reader about the various model's performance and the architecture of famous LLM's like ChatGPT, Qwen, DeepSeek, and Claude, along with their comparisons. In the course of this article, we have provided plenty of knowledge about LLMs, which can provide a framework for researchers and may clear paths for them.

articleTitle: Integration of Generative AI and Image Fusion for Enhanced Brain Tumor Detection in PET-MRI Data
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This study introduces a novel generative AI-driven system for brain tumor detection by integrating PET and MRI data through an advanced image fusion approach. The fused images were used for training on the machine in the real-world dataset. It provided very high sensitivity and specificity with a sensitivity of 98.7 and a specificity of 99.2%. Ablation experiments with statistical analysis demonstrated the superiority of the system along with its robustness with other existing models. The viability of the technology for healthcare applications was also illustrated through real-time implementation through an intuitive interface. This research introduces a novel approach to diagnosing brain malignancies using multimodal imaging to set new benchmarks for accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: Enhancing Women's Security with Real-Time Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This project introduces an innovative solution aimed at improving women's safety through real-time monitoring, combining advanced technologies to offer thorough protection and emergency response. The system is based on an Arduino microcontroller that processes data from a range of sensors. The ESP32 camera enables live video streaming, allowing remote observation of the user's environment. MEMS and force sensors are designed to detect abnormal movements or potential dangers, such as sudden falls or physical force, activating emergency alerts when necessary. Voice recognition technology is integrated to interpret specific commands, sending automatic notifications to emergency contacts or authorities. Furthermore, the heartbeat sensor tracks the user's health, while the GPS module provides accurate location data for real-time tracking during emergencies. In urgent situations, a shock mechanism can be triggered for self-defense. A push button is included to manually activate an emergency alert, especially in case of system failure or when immediate action is needed. A relay controls power distribution to the system's components, while an LCD display and buzzer provide immediate feedback and alerts. The GSM module sends SMS alerts to emergency contacts.

articleTitle: Comparing Different Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models for Daily Rainfall Prediction at Kerala Point Location
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Accurate prediction of daily rainfall is crucial for water resource management, disaster preparedness, and agricultural planning in monsoon-prone regions such as Kerala. Traditional statistical models cannot capture the nonlinear nature of the rainfall patterns. This paper attempts to compare various Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) models, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), XGBoost, LightGBM, and Gradient Boosting, to assess the performance of daily rainfall forecasting at a Kerala point location. Using historical rainfall data, from 1981 to 2023, The models were trained, tested, and evaluated for performance based on the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Results: Deep learning approaches especially LSTM perform very well and outshine the traditional approaches and capture temporal dependencies Also the ensemble approach has a maximum predictive accuracy, thus the hybrid approach can be useful for rainfall time series forecasting. This research focuses on the benefits of advanced learning techniques in weather prediction and gives suggestions for future improvements, including real-time meteorological data integration.

articleTitle: ECG Data Mining Approach for Detection of Arrhythmia Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The Electrocardiogram (ECG) is very important signal generated from human body that provides information for assessment of variation in cardiac activities. These ECG data are generally distorted due to high power line or magnetic field associated noise that results as a problem in error during diagnosis of heart related disorders on analysis through biomedical analysis software. This work contributes for very significant stage that is introduced to reduce the anomaly in the ECG signals to perform accurate automated diagnosis. This work follows a methodology of an automated machine learning algorithm is developed for accurate estimation of ECG data segment cycle using clustering approach integrated with Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). The key findings of this works cover the development and analysis of an approach to overcome the errors in detection of T-wave using Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillator (ICD). The work reports the solution of issues using fuzzy C-means clustering behind prediction of fatal Ventricular Arrhythmias (VA) for performing standard classifications.

articleTitle: Implementing an Intelligent Irrigation System in Oman Using Machine Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In this study, machine-learning technique is used to collect environmental data in real time and measures other aspects like soil moisture, temperature, water level, humidity. Water use efficiency has recently increased because to new agricultural techniques, sophisticated sensors as Micro Controller, and Wireless Sensor Network (WSN). Irrigation Fault Detection method based on XGBoost (IFD-XGBoost) Algorithm used as proposed method as robust to missing values imputing them naturally during tree splitting. The Suggested method is optimized for speed, using parallel and distributed computing to make predictions faster compare to other Regression Algorithm and avoid over fitting. Using Min-Max Normalization, features with different sizes and units can affect the efficacy of several machine learning algorithms. By warping the statistical relationship between features, removal of noisy data and error detection can reduce the machine learning models' efficiency. Lasso Regression is a linear model that combines regularization and feature selection. Additionally, less data will be kept in the centralized cloud as a result. Using the IFD-XGBoost Algorithm's ability to handle missing data, learn from past errors, and adjust parameters, our proposed approach would be the best model to implement. It outperform from other algorithm in Predictive accuracy, making it reliable for calculating water needs and forecasting weather. Investigating the implementation of several machine learning models that can offer the best real-world irrigation decision management is the main goal of this article. The comparative analysis to evaluate the IFD-XGBoost method yielded a minimum RMSE of 0.3524, MAE of 0.1832, MAPE of 4.24 with the highest accuracy of 99.2%, precision of 96.2% and AUC-ROC of 95%, indicates when combined, these metrics provide insightful data about each model's ability to anticipate future developments in irrigation systems.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: GPS-Independent Indoor Navigation-Enabled Autonomous Wheeled Robot with Obstacle Avoidance
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In certain situations, GPS-based wheeled robots are ineffective in places where GPS signals are unavailable or unreliable, such as remote areas and indoor spaces. As a result, GPS independent autonomous wheeled robots are gaining importance for applications like warehouse management, autonomous delivery, healthcare assistance, smart building automation, indoor transportation systems, and robotic assistance for elderly or disabled individuals. This paper proposes a GPS independent navigation system for wheeled robots, enabling them to autonomously follow predefined paths and to strategically avoid obstacles during its mobility. The robot modifies its route in real-time, according to obstacle detection. The wheeled robot utilizes linear regression machine learning technique to predict and avoid future obstacles. The system incorporates ultrasonic sensors for obstacle detection, wheel encoders to track wheel rotations and distance traveled, and a gyroscope for orientation control. This allows the robot to detect changes in its rotational movement and to correct its mobility or direction accordingly. By dynamically adjusting the wheeled robot's path and travel time based on sensor inputs, the system ensures smooth navigation in cluttered or remote environments. Obtained Experimental results indicates that our proposed navigation model outperforms existing systems in path efficiency and obstacle avoidance, offering a more reliable and efficient GPS-independent navigation solution.

articleTitle: Improvement of Power Quality of On-Board Charger for Electrical Vehicular Applications: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In this paper, we give a thorough classification of power quality (PQ) enhancement strategies for OBCs in light of electric vehicle (EV) applications. With the scroll to EVs gathers momentum, so does the demand for smart and trustworthy charging mechanism. With their involvement in charging batteries by converting the grid's ac power to dc power, OBCs are crucial to the process, and poorly designed OBCs can harm grid stability and system efficiency. Nevertheless, keeping high PQ standards is a challenge due to problems that include harmonic distortion, low power factor, electromagnetic interference (EMI), as well as transient events. This paper reviews some of the solutions, such as active and passive filtering, power factor correction (PFC) methods and advanced converter topologies to mitigate these problems. It reviews trends towards boosting efficiency and minimize losses with wide-bandgap (WBG) materials such as gallium nitride (GaN) and silicon carbide (SiC), as well as emerging trends like bidirectional OBCs and wireless power transfer (WPT). Furthermore, the potential for improved PQ in future OBC systems through the integration of renewable energy sources and AI-based control strategies is also assessed. This review aims to highlight current gaps and future directions that will contribute to the establishment of sustainable and efficient EV charging infrastructure.

articleTitle: Implementation of Deep Learning Algorithm to Estimate the State of Charge (SOC) of Lithium Ion Battery
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In electric vehicles (EVs), the need for superior battery management systems (BMS) to confirm efficiency, maximum performance of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) and safety is increasing. Accurate evaluation of state of charge (SOC) is essential to avoid overcharge and over discharge, which can degrade the battery health and performance. Conventional techniques for estimating SOC often struggle with the nonlinearities and temporal complexities of LIB dynamics, make necessary adoption of advanced machine learning techniques. To enhance the SOC estimation, this analysis suggests a combined Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) model to ensure the accuracy under dynamic operating conditions. CNNs are adapt at extracting spatial features from battery data, while GRUs excel in modeling sequential dependencies. The combined CNN-GRU architecture leverages the complementary strengths of both models, providing robust predictions that address the limitations of standalone frameworks. The performance of this model is measured using dataset based on the widely used model like Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) in data network. The CNN-GRU model performs far better than the LSTM model, based on the experimental data, with lower Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). The CNN-GRU's capability to record both local as well as global temporal patterns results in the reduced prediction deviations, particularly during rapid SOC transitions. Analysis of training and validation losses further highlights the CNN-GRU's generalization capability, with stable convergence and minimal overfitting. This analysis underscores the potential of hybrid architectures in advancing intelligent BMS design. By integrating efficient feature extraction and sequence modeling, the CNN-GRU framework ensures accurate and robust SOC estimation and real-time performance.

articleTitle: Mod-ViT: A Vision Transformer-Based Framework for Breast Cancer Detection from Multiple Imaging Modalities
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The evaluation of breast cancer plays a crucial role in its diagnosis through various imaging modalities. Although Convolutional Neural Network-based deep learning (DL) methods have significantly advanced this process, they are hindered by high computational demands and restricted spatial encoding capabilities. In contrast, Vision Transformer-based DL offers a compelling alternative due to its superior ability to encode spatial information efficiently. This study presents a breast cancer detection framework using a modified vision transformer (Mod- ViT) architecture across four publicly available datasets; mammogram (InBreast and MIAS) and ultrasound (BUSI and Mendeley). The workflow involves three key stages: data collection, image preprocessing, and classification. Mod- ViT utilizes transfer learning by modifying the pretrained vision transformer with additional layers, including flattening, batch normalization, dense, dropout, and a fully connected classification layer. The proposed Mod- ViT model was evaluated on each dataset, yielding superior performance metrics compared to VGG-16, ResNet-50, and VGG-19. On the InBreast dataset, Mod-ViT achieved 98.74% accuracy, 96.54% precision, 97.62% recall, and 98.25% F1-score, highlighting its ability to capture global mammogram features effectively. Similarly, on MIAS, BUSI, and Mendeley datasets, Mod- ViT consistently outperformed other models with accuracies of 99.92 %, 98.61 %, and 99.31 %, respectively. These results demonstrate Mod-ViT's robustness in classifying benign, malignant, and normal cases across diverse imaging modalities. By employing advanced attention mechanisms and effectively processing spatial and contextual information, Mod- ViT has shown its capability to address the complexities of breast cancer detection. This work highlights the promise of transformer-based models in enhancing diagnostic precision and reliability in medical imaging.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Machine Learning Framework for Ground Water Level Prediction in Peatland Ecosystems
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Peatland ecosystems are important for biodiversity and carbon storage, but they are vulnerable to fluctuations in the water table leading to improper environmental health and agricultural productivity. Accurate and timely Ground Water Level (GWL) predictions are necessary to overcome these challenges. The research presents an IoT-based machine learning-enabled framework for predicting the GWL, using real-time IoT sensor data on soil moisture, temperature, and atmospheric pressure. The system uses sophisticated algorithms in its analysis of data to predict GWL with great accuracy using Random Forest and LSTM. Thus, the system ensures timely alerts for stakeholders to manage peatland water resources effectively by being cost-effective and scalable.
