The real-time monitoring and predictive insights offered may also allow it to eventually integrate with the irrigation system for proactive intervention. All these approaches aim to enhance peatland management, reduce environmental degradation, and support sustainable agricultural practices with incentives for preserving ecological stability and economic resilience.

articleTitle: Enhancing Lung Cancer Detection: A Framework for Lung Parenchyma Segmentation and Classification Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Lung cancer continues to be one of the most prevalent causes of cancer-related fatalities worldwide, with a high mortality rate attributed to late-stage diagnosis. Early detection is essential for enhancing patient outcomes, as it enables the implementation of appropriate therapies that can substantially increase survival rates. In the past few years, artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods have emerged as powerful instruments to assist radiologists, enabling them to conduct diagnoses that are more consistent, efficient, and accurate. This study introduces a comprehensive framework for the detection of lung cancer that combines deep learning models with advanced segmentation techniques, utilizing CT images. This framework implements techniques such as data augmentation, segmentation techniques, and transfer learning to improve diagnostic accuracy by addressing critical issues such as class imbalance and juxtapleural nodule segmentation. Among the models tested, ResNet50 outperformed EfficientNetB0, DenseNet121, and VGG16, achieving an F1 score of 93. 10% and an accuracy of 93. 04%.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Overview of HEMT Structure and Fabrication Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive overview of high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs), exploring the structural design and fabrication techniques that underpin their high-performance applications in power and high-frequency domains. The discussion begins with a detailed analysis of each HEMT layer, from the substrate to the encapsulation layers, explaining the role each plays in optimizing electron mobility, thermal management, and power efficiency. Various materials used in HEMTs, including AlGaN/GaN, AlGaAs/GaAs, InAlAs/InGaAs, and GaN-on-Si, are examined to highlight their distinct benefits and challenges in different operational contexts. Additionally, the paper outlines key fabrication processes like epitaxial growth, lithography, and metallization, which contribute to the HEMT's structural integrity and functional reliability. The insights provided aim to advance the understanding of HEMT architecture, paving the way for further innovation in electronic devices that require robust, efficient, and high-speed semiconductor technologies.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Hybrid V2X Communication and Edge Processing Techniques for Real-Time Emergency Vehicle Detection and Prioritization in Urban Traffic Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This review paper presents the use of hybrid Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication systems to detect and prioritize emergency vehicles in congested urban areas. To reduce response times, researchers are merging edge processing with Dedicated Short-Range Communication (DSRC) and Cellular Vehicle-to-Everything (C-V2X). The technology provides extremely fast, low-latency connections, which are essential for real-time applications, by utilizing recent developments in 5G and edge computing. To increase detection accuracy in noisy urban settings, researchers are experimenting with multi-sensor fusion systems that combine GPS, acoustic sensors, and AI-powered vision. Adaptive traffic signal preemption algorithms that dynamically modify traffic flows to grant priority access to emergency vehicles are also being investigated in some research. Despite its promise, there are still obstacles to be addressed, such as interoperability problems and network congestion. However, the benefits might be enormous: quicker emergency reactions, more seamless traffic patterns, and generally more effective urban transportation systems. In the upcoming years, we should witness some fascinating breakthroughs as researchers continue to hone these technologies.

articleTitle: Enhanced Thermal Object Tracking in Search and Rescue Missions Using Adaptive 3D Kalman Filtering
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Search and rescue (SAR) operations often involve hazardous environments where rapid human detection is critical for survival. While thermal imaging drones have improved SAR capabilities, challenges persist in maintaining accurate tracking amid dynamic environmental conditions, occlusions, and changing perspectives. This paper presents a novel approach to thermal human tracking by implementing an adaptive 3D Kalman filtering system integrated with depth estimation techniques. Our methodology enhances tracking accuracy by extending traditional 2D Kalman filters to incorporate altitude changes and advanced occlusion handling. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in detection reliability and tracking persistence across challenging scenarios including darkness, smoke, and dense foliage. The system achieves 92% detection accuracy in low-visibility conditions and reduces false positive rates by 37% compared to conventional methods. This research addresses critical gaps in SAR technology while offering applications across disaster management, wildlife conservation, and industrial safety domains. The proposed framework enables more efficient SAR operations, potentially reducing response times and improving survival outcomes in disaster scenarios.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach to Feature Selection for Cyber Threat Detection in IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The quick expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) devices have greatly impact multiple sectors, including healthcare, smart agriculture, and environmental monitoring, thereby impacting human lives. The heterogeneous nature and limited resources of these devices make them highly vulnerable to cyber threats. To address these security challenges, machine learning plays a significant role in the development of adaptive intrusion detection systems. Machine learning helps in identifying patterns from the vast amounts of data produced through different IoT devices, particularly for enhancing security. It facilitates in identifying assaults by analyzing trends and abnormalities in data that indicate threats, offering a proactive strategy for cyber security. In this study, we have explored the impact of different Methods of feature selection on the effectiveness of machine learning models in detection of IoT attacks. Feature Selection Methods such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Autoencoders (AE), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) and a hybrid selection method combining SelectKBest and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) are employed to asses different machine learning models. The UNSW-NB15 dataset is used to evaluate the effectiveness of Random Forest (RF), XGBoost and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers. The experimental results indicate that the hybrid feature selection approach considerably improves classification efficiency, particularly for the RF model which outperform the other having accuracy 99.91%, surpassing traditional dimensionality reduction techniques. The suggested approach effectively eliminates redundant attributes while retaining the most informative elements, leading to improved detection accuracy and other performance metrics. These findings underscore the practical applicability of hybrid feature selection techniques in cyber security, offering a scalable and efficient solution for IoT attack detection.

articleTitle: An Effective Method for the Detection of Tuberculosis Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), remains a significant global health challenge, is one of the deadliest diseases in the world, is affecting millions of people, especially in low and middle-income countries. The early detection of this disease is still a big problem to the affected due to the lack of technology used for detecting the disease at an earlier stage in the medical paradigm. One of the most frequently used screening tools is the chest X-ray (CXR) because it is non-invasive and prevents penetration to diagnose the disease. Even if this technique is non-invasive, the proper diagnosis is done with the help of expert radiologists; otherwise, human error is produced, and efficiency will be reduced. The main objective of this research work is to propose an Artificial Intelligence (AI) -based technique for the detection of TB through the automated analysis of chest X-rays. In this scenario, a new scheme using deep neural learning, especially Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), has been employed for high accuracy and specificity for classifying TB and normal subjects. The performance of the proposed system is analyzed with five parameters, mainly accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity and F1 score, used as diagnostic parameters for the disease diagnosis. This system can be used as a benchmark against the existing methods of TB detection and analysis. In addition to the above, this work help the subjects to improve their results in the diagnosis of TB using CXR and AI technology.

articleTitle: IOT Based Sustainable Waste Separation and Alert System
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Waste separation and monitoring have emerged as an innovative solution in contemporary waste management through the integration of sensors, Arduino microcontrollers, and IoT connectivity. This amalgamation of technologies signifies a significant departure from traditional waste collection methods, offering real-time monitoring and automated functionalities. By precisely segregating waste into metal, wet, dry, and plastic categories, these bins streamline recycling endeavors and mitigate environmental repercussions. The incorporation of WiFi and GSM modules facilitates seamless communication with municipal authorities, enabling data-driven decision-making for optimized waste collection routes and resource allocation. The adoption of smart dustbins is imperative for fostering cleaner, more sustainable urban environments by augmenting operational efficiency and curtailing expenses. Furthermore, these advancements cultivate environmental awareness, prompting active engagement in recycling initiatives. Ultimately, smart dustbins epitomize a paradigm shift in waste management, encapsulating principles of efficiency, sustainability, and technological advancement for a greener future.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Fault Detection in VLSI Circuits
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper addresses the growing complexity of electronic devices and the need for efficient fault detection in VLSI circuits. Traditional fault detection methods are often inaccurate and time-consuming, motivating the use of artificial intelligence techniques. The paper proposes a deep learning-based model for detecting stuck-at faults in digital VLSI circuits. Our model leverages an Autoencoder algorithm to compress features and mitigate the search space explosion problem, achieving a range of accuracies of 75.3% to 99.9% for various ISCAS'85 benchmark circuits. The model incorporates ATPG tools such as the ATALANTA tool for generating test patterns and corresponding fault-free responses using the FAN algorithm. These test patterns are preprocessed to be used as a dataset where the Autoencoder algorithm classifies faulty and non-faulty responses based on their reconstruction error. These approaches demonstrate the potential of deep learning in improving the efficiency and accuracy of fault detection in digital VLSI circuits.

articleTitle: Exploring Explainable AI in Brain Tumor Detection: A Hybrid Approach Using EfficientNet and CBAM
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This research presents an advanced methodology for brain tumour classification using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), combining the EfficientNet-B0 architecture with Convolutional Block Attention Modules (CBAM). The proposed model effectively captures both channel and spatial attention by replacing the Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) modules with CBAM, enhancing feature extraction and classification accuracy. The framework is evaluated on a comprehensive dataset comprising four classes: pituitary no tumour, meningioma, and glioma. Leveraging transfer learning and Grad-CAM-based explainability, the proposed model attains an outstanding accuracy of 99%, with weighted F1 score and macro scores exceeding 98%. Comparative analyses confirm its superior performance against state-of-the-art methods, particularly in classifying complex tumour types. The combination of accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability highlights the potential of this approach for real-world medical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Optimization of Network Security Protocols for Enhanced Threat Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Current cyber threats are relatively sophisticated, and this has put pressure on traditional network security protocols. It proposes an extended machine learning methodology using a supervised Random Forest algorithm for classification and an unsupervised Autoencoder for anomaly detection to improve network security measures. The consumes network traffic through a powerful preprocessing pipeline of feature selection, scaling, and encoding to increase the performance of a model. The proposed method was also tested on benchmark datasets like CICIDS2017, UNSW-NB15, and KDDCup99 with an accuracy of 98.76%, precision of 96.45%, false positive rate under 1.89%, and a latency of only 4.23ms better than other methods from 2021, 2022 and 2023. These results show that the ability of the developed framework is higher in terms of detection and more adaptable to real-world threats. It offers a transportable and secure solution for next-generation networks, which overcomes the gaps of the previous methods to make way for further developments.

articleTitle: 5G Wireless Network Security: Investigating Next-Generation Mobile Communication Data Encryption Methods and Authentication Protocols
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Unprecedented levels of speed, capacity, and connectivity for billions of devices are all on the horizon with the introduction of 5G wireless networks, which constitute a significant leap in mobile communication technology. These improvements, however, bring with them significant security concerns that need to be addressed in order to protect sensitive data and guarantee the privacy of users. This study analyzes the data encryption methods and authentication protocols that are specifically created for 5G networks, which are specifically designed for the next generation of mobile communication. To begin, we conduct an analysis of the inherent weaknesses that are present in the wireless communication systems that are now in use. This analysis drives home the point that robust encryption mechanisms are required to protect against unwanted access and data breaches. Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC), Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), and homomorphic encryption are some of the advanced algorithms that are discussed in our research paper. A variety of encryption methods that are designed for 5G architecture are also discussed. As part of the 5G ecosystem, we evaluate how well they are able to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity of data while taking into account the limitations imposed by devices with limited resources. Further, we investigate novel authentication protocols, such as Mutual Authentication and Enhanced Authentication and Key Agreement (EAKA), which are designed to improve the level of security that is present during the interaction between the user and the network equipment. In order to evaluate the effectiveness, efficiency, and resilience of these encryption algorithms and authentication procedures in the face of growing threats in the 5G landscape, we conduct a series of simulations and comparative data analysis. Compared to earlier generations, the findings indicate a significant improvement in the security characteristics, and specific recommendations have been provided for the application of these protocols in order to strengthen the entire security framework of 5G networks. Furthermore, our findings provide a road map for future research and development in the field of 5G wireless network security, which is a contribution to the ongoing discussion on the topic of protecting mobile communications of the next generation.
